title.en: Volume 74 Biographies 12: Zong Han Formerly Named Zhanhan, Son: Xiege, Zong Wang Formerly Named Wo Libu, Sons: Qi, Jing, Wen
title.raw: 卷七十四 列傳第十二: 宗翰本名粘罕 子:斜哥 宗望本名斡離不 子:齊 京 文 Volume 74 Biographies 12: Zong Han Formerly Named Zhanhan, Son: Xiege, Zong Wang Formerly Named Wo Libu, Sons: Qi, Jing, Wen

sentences.zh: 列傳第十二 ○宗翰本名粘罕 子:斜哥 宗望本名斡離不 子:齊 京 文

translations.literal: Biography 12 ○ Zong Han (original name Zhanhan), son: Xiege; Zong Wang (original name Wo Libu), sons: Qi, Jing, Wen
translations.idiomatic: Biography 12: Zong Han (original name Zhanhan); his son Xiege; Zong Wang (original name Wo Libu); his sons Qi, Jing, and Wen

sentences.zh: 宗翰本名粘沒喝，漢語訛為粘罕，國相撒改之長子也。

translations.literal: Zong Han's original name was Nianmohan; in Chinese speech this was corrupted to Zhanhan. He was the eldest son of the chief minister Sagai.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han's original name was Nianmohan, which Chinese speakers corrupted to Zhanhan. He was the eldest son of Chief Minister Sagai.

sentences.zh: 年十七，軍中服其勇。

translations.literal: At age seventeen, the army respected his bravery.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of seventeen, the troops already respected his courage.

sentences.zh: 及議伐遼，宗翰與太祖意合。

translations.literal: When they discussed attacking Liao, Zong Han agreed with the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated attacking Liao, Zong Han's views matched those of the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖敗遼師於境上，獲耶律謝十。

translations.literal: The Taizu defeated Liao forces at the border and captured Yelü Xieshi.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu defeated Liao troops on the frontier and captured Yelü Xieshi.

sentences.zh: 撒改使宗翰及完顏希尹來賀捷，即稱帝為賀。

translations.literal: Sagai sent Zong Han and Wanyan Xiyin to congratulate the victory, addressing him as Emperor in the congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Sagai sent Zong Han and Wanyan Xiyin to congratulate the victory, and in doing so addressed him as emperor.

sentences.zh: 及太宗以下宗室群臣皆勸進，太祖猶謙讓。

translations.literal: When Taizong and the other imperial clansmen and ministers all urged accession, the Taizu still demurred.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong and the other princes and ministers all urged him to take the throne, the Taizu still held back.

sentences.zh: 宗翰與阿離合懣、蒲家奴等進曰：「若不以時建號，無以系天下心。」

translations.literal: Zong Han with Aliehemen, Pujianu, and others advanced and said: "If you do not establish a title in season, there is no way to bind the hearts of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han, Aliehemen, Pujianu, and others stepped forward and said, "If you do not establish your title at the right moment, you cannot win the hearts of the realm."

sentences.zh: 太祖意乃決。

translations.literal: Only then did the Taizu decide.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the Taizu make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 遼都統耶律訛裏朵以二十余萬戍邊，太祖逆擊之，宗翰為右軍，大敗遼人于達魯古城。

translations.literal: Liao commander-in-chief Yelü Woliduo with more than two hundred thousand guarded the border. The Taizu met and attacked him; Zong Han was the right wing and greatly defeated the Liao at Dalugu City.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao commander-in-chief Yelü Woliduo stationed more than two hundred thousand men on the border. The Taizu marched out to meet him; Zong Han commanded the right wing and routed the Liao at Dalugu City.

sentences.zh: 天輔五年四月，宗翰奏曰：「遼主失德，中外離心。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Tianfu, Zong Han memorialized: "The Liao ruler has lost virtue; within and without, hearts are estranged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianfu 5, Zong Han submitted a memorial: "The Liao ruler has lost the Way, and court and country alike have turned away from him.

sentences.zh: 我朝興師，大業既定，而根本弗除，後必為患。

translations.literal: Our dynasty has raised troops and the great enterprise is settled, yet the root is not removed; later it will surely become a trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty has taken the field and the great enterprise is already assured, but if we do not uproot them at the source, they will trouble us again.

sentences.zh: 今乘其釁，可襲取之。

translations.literal: Now, seizing their opening, we can strike and take them.
translations.idiomatic: Now, while their weakness is exposed, we can strike and seize them.

sentences.zh: 天時人事，不可失也。」

translations.literal: Heaven's season and human affairs—this must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's timing and human opportunity must not be missed."

sentences.zh: 太祖然之，即命諸路戒備軍事。

translations.literal: The Taizu approved this and immediately ordered all routes to ready military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu agreed and at once ordered every route to prepare for war.

sentences.zh: 五月戊戌，射柳，宴群臣。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day of the fifth month, he shot at the willow and feasted the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the fifth month, he held the willow-shooting rite and feasted his ministers.

sentences.zh: 上顧謂宗翰曰：「今議西征，汝前後計議多合朕意。

translations.literal: The sovereign turned and said to Zong Han: "Now that we discuss the western campaign, your plans before and after have largely matched my intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Zong Han and said, "As we discuss the western campaign, your proposals have again and again matched my intent.

sentences.zh: 宗室中雖有長於汝者，若謀元帥，無以易汝。

translations.literal: Although among the imperial clan there are those older than you, if we choose a commander, none can replace you.
translations.idiomatic: Even if some in the imperial clan outrank you in age, when it comes to choosing a commander, no one can take your place.

sentences.zh: 汝當治兵，以俟師期。」

translations.literal: You should ready the troops and await the date of the army's departure."
translations.idiomatic: You must ready the troops and wait for the day the army marches."

sentences.zh: 上親酌酒飲之，且命之釂，解禦衣以衣之。

translations.literal: The sovereign personally poured wine for him to drink, ordered him to toast in return, and removed his own robe to clothe him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally poured wine for him, commanded him to drink a toast in return, and took off his own robe to dress him in it.

sentences.zh: 群臣言時方暑月，乃止。

translations.literal: The ministers said it was then the height of summer, and so he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers said it was the height of summer, and on that account he desisted.

sentences.zh: 無何，為移賚勃極烈，副蒲家奴西襲遼帝，不果行。

translations.literal: Before long he became Yisai Bojilie, assisting Pujianu in a western strike against the Liao emperor, but the plan was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Yisai Bojilie and was to assist Pujianu in a western strike against the Liao emperor, but the campaign did not take place.

sentences.zh: 十一月，宗翰複請曰：「諸軍久駐，人思自奮，馬亦壯健，宜乘此時進取中京。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Zong Han again petitioned: "The armies have long been encamped; the men wish to exert themselves, and the horses too are strong. We should seize this moment to take Central Capital."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zong Han petitioned again: "The armies have been encamped a long time; the men are eager to fight, and the horses are in fine condition. We ought to seize this moment and take Central Capital."

sentences.zh: 群臣言時方寒，太祖不聽，竟用宗翰策。

translations.literal: The ministers said it was then cold, and the Taizu did not listen; in the end he adopted Zong Han's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers said the season was already cold, but the Taizu would not heed them and in the end adopted Zong Han's plan.

sentences.zh: 於是，忽魯勃極烈杲都統內外諸軍，蒲家奴、宗翰、宗幹、宗磐副之，宗峻領合紮猛安，皆受金牌，餘睹為鄉導，取中京實北京。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huru Bojilie Gao commanded all forces within and without; Pujianu, Zong Han, Zong Gan, and Zong Pan were his deputies; Zong Jun led the combined Zha Meng'an; all received gold tablets; Yudu served as guide; they took Central Capital, which was Northern Capital in fact.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Huru Bojilie Gao took overall command of the armies; Pujianu, Zong Han, Zong Gan, and Zong Pan served as his deputies; Zong Jun led the combined Zha Meng'an forces; all received gold command tablets; Yudu acted as guide; and they captured Central Capital, the true Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 既克中京，宗翰率偏師趨北安州，與婁室、徒單綽裏合兵，大敗奚王霞末，北安遂降。

translations.literal: After Central Capital was taken, Zong Han led a detached force toward Bei'an Prefecture, joined forces with Wushi and Tushan Chuli, and greatly defeated the Xi king Xiamo; Bei'an then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After Central Capital fell, Zong Han led a detached column toward Bei'an Prefecture, joined Wushi and Tushan Chuli, and routed the Xi king Xiamo; Bei'an then submitted.

sentences.zh: 宗翰駐軍北安，遣希尹經略近地，獲遼護衛耶律習泥烈，乃知遼主獵於鴛鴦濼，殺其子晉王敖魯斡，眾益離心，西北、西南兩路兵馬皆羸弱，不可用。

translations.literal: Zong Han encamped at Bei'an and sent Xiyin to secure the nearby region. They captured Liao guard Yelü Xinilie and then learned that the Liao ruler was hunting at Yuanyang Marsh, had killed his son the Prince of Jin Aoluwo, and that the people were ever more estranged; the armies of the northwest and southwest routes were all weak and could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han encamped at Bei'an and sent Xiyin to secure the nearby country. They captured the Liao guard Yelü Xinilie and learned that the Liao emperor was hunting at Yuanyang Marsh, had killed his son the Prince of Jin Aoluwo, and that morale was collapsing; the troops on the northwest and southwest routes were all feeble and useless.

sentences.zh: 宗翰使耨碗溫都、移刺保報都統杲曰：「遼主窮迫於山西，猶事畋獵，不恤危亡，自殺其子，臣民失望。

translations.literal: Zong Han sent Nouwan Wendu and Yila Bao to report to Commander Gao: "The Liao ruler, hard pressed in Shanxi, still goes hunting, heedless of peril, and has killed his own son; officials and people have lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han sent Nouwan Wendu and Yila Bao to report to Commander Gao: "The Liao emperor, driven to the wall in Shanxi, still goes hunting and cares nothing for ruin; he has killed his own son, and officials and people alike have lost heart.

sentences.zh: 攻取之策，幸速見諭。

translations.literal: A plan to attack and take him—may you quickly instruct us.
translations.idiomatic: Please send us your instructions at once on how we should strike and take him.

sentences.zh: 若有異議，此當以偏師討之。」

translations.literal: If there is disagreement, this wing will use a detached force to subdue him."
translations.idiomatic: If you disagree, this wing will move against him with a detached force alone."

sentences.zh: 杲使奔睹與移刺保同來報曰：「頃奉詔旨，不令便趨山西，當審詳徐議。」

translations.literal: Gao sent Bendu and Yila Bao back together to report: "We have just received the imperial order not to hurry toward Shanxi; we should deliberate carefully and proceed slowly."
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent Bendu back with Yila Bao to reply: "We have just received orders not to press into Shanxi at once; the matter must be weighed carefully and discussed at length."

sentences.zh: 當時，宗翰使人報杲，即整眾俟兵期。

translations.literal: At that time Zong Han had sent men to report to Gao and was already marshaling the host awaiting the date of the army's march.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zong Han had already sent word to Gao and was marshaling his troops, waiting for the day the army was to march.

sentences.zh: 及奔睹至，知杲無意進取，宗翰恐待杲約或失機會，即決策進兵。

translations.literal: When Bendu arrived, knowing that Gao had no intent to advance, Zong Han feared that waiting for Gao's agreement might lose the opportunity and immediately decided to advance the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Bendu arrived and Zong Han saw that Gao had no intention of advancing, he feared that waiting on Gao's word would cost them the moment and at once resolved to march.

sentences.zh: 使移刺保複往報都統曰：「初受命雖未令便取山西，亦許便宜從事。

translations.literal: He sent Yila Bao again to report to the commander: "At first, though the command did not order us to take Shanxi at once, we were also permitted to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yila Bao back to the commander with word: "Though our first orders did not tell us to seize Shanxi immediately, we were also allowed to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 遼人可取，其勢已見，一失機會，後難圖矣。

translations.literal: The Liao can be taken; the situation is already clear. Once the opportunity is lost, it will be hard to achieve later.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao can be taken—the signs are already plain. Miss this chance and we will not get another.

sentences.zh: 今已進兵，當與大軍會于何地，幸以見報。」

translations.literal: We have now advanced the army; at what place should we join the main force? May you report this."
translations.idiomatic: We have already advanced. Where should we join the main army? Please let us know."

sentences.zh: 宗幹勸杲當如宗翰策，杲意乃決，約以奚王嶺會議。

translations.literal: Zong Gan urged Gao to follow Zong Han's plan; Gao's mind was then decided, and they agreed to confer at Xiwang Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Gan urged Gao to follow Zong Han's plan; Gao's mind was made up, and they agreed to confer at Xiwang Ridge.

sentences.zh: 宗翰至奚王嶺，與都統杲會。

translations.literal: Zong Han reached Xiwang Ridge and met with Commander Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han reached Xiwang Ridge and met Commander Gao.

sentences.zh: 杲軍出青嶺，宗翰軍出瓢嶺，期於羊城濼會軍。

translations.literal: Gao's army came out by Qing Ridge, Zong Han's army by Piao Ridge; they set a rendezvous at Yangcheng Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's army marched out through Qing Ridge and Zong Han's through Piao Ridge; they agreed to join forces at Yangcheng Marsh.

sentences.zh: 宗翰以精兵六千襲遼主，聞遼主自五院司來拒戰，宗翰倍道兼行，一宿而至，遼主遁去。

translations.literal: Zong Han with six thousand elite troops struck at the Liao ruler. Hearing that the Liao ruler was coming from the Five Yuan Office to resist, Zong Han doubled his march; in one night he arrived, and the Liao ruler fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han took six thousand picked troops to strike at the Liao emperor. Learning that the emperor was coming from the Five Yuan Office to give battle, he forced the march and arrived in a single night; the Liao emperor fled.

sentences.zh: 乃使希尹等追之。

translations.literal: He then sent Xiyin and others in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Xiyin and others in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 西京複叛，耿守忠以兵五千來救，至城東四十里，蒲察烏烈、穀赧先擊之，斬首千餘。

translations.literal: Western Capital rebelled again. Geng Shouzhong came to the rescue with five thousand troops. When they reached forty li east of the city, Pucha Wulie and Gunan struck them first and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Western Capital rebelled again. Geng Shouzhong marched to its relief with five thousand men. Forty li east of the city, Pucha Wulie and Gunan struck first and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 宗翰、宗雄、宗幹、宗峻繼至，宗翰率麾下自其中衝擊之，使余兵去馬從旁射之。

translations.literal: Zong Han, Zong Xiong, Zong Gan, and Zong Jun arrived in succession. Zong Han led his personal followers in a charge through the center and ordered the remaining troops to dismount and shoot from the flanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han, Zong Xiong, Zong Gan, and Zong Jun came up in turn. Zong Han led his household troops in a charge through the center while the rest dismounted and shot from the flanks.

sentences.zh: 守忠敗走，其眾殲焉。

translations.literal: Shouzhong was defeated and fled; his host was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong was beaten and fled; his force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 宗翰弟紮保迪沒於陣。

translations.literal: Zong Han's younger brother Zhabaodi perished in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han's younger brother Zhabaodi fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 天眷中，贈紮保迪特進雲。

translations.literal: In the Tianjuan era he was posthumously granted Zhabaodi the title Tejin Yun.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjuan era Zhabaodi was posthumously granted the title Tejin Yun.

sentences.zh: 宗翰已撫定西路州縣部族，謁上於行在所，遂從上取燕京。

translations.literal: Zong Han had already pacified the prefectures, counties, and tribes of the western route, paid homage to the sovereign at the traveling palace, and then followed the sovereign in taking Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han had already pacified the western prefectures, counties, and tribal districts. He paid homage to the emperor at the traveling palace and then followed him in the capture of Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 燕京平，賜宗翰、希尹、撻懶、耶律余睹金器有差。

translations.literal: When Yanjing was pacified, Zong Han, Xiyin, Tawan, and Yelü Yudu were granted gold vessels in differing measure.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanjing was pacified, Zong Han, Xiyin, Tawan, and Yelü Yudu were rewarded with gold vessels in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 太祖既以燕京與宋人，還軍次鴛鴦濼，不豫，將歸京師。

translations.literal: After the Taizu had given Yanjing to the Song, the army returned and halted at Yuanyang Marsh. He was unwell and was about to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu had handed Yanjing to the Song, the army withdrew and encamped at Yuanyang Marsh. The emperor fell ill and prepared to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以宗翰為都統，昃勃極烈昱、迭勃極烈斡魯副之，駐軍雲中。

translations.literal: He appointed Zong Han commander-in-chief, with Yisai Bojilie Yu and Die Bojilie Wolu as deputies, and stationed the army at Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zong Han commander-in-chief, with Yisai Bojilie Yu and Die Bojilie Wolu as his deputies, and stationed the army at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 諸將獲耶律馬哥，宗翰歸之京師。

translations.literal: The generals captured Yelü Mage; Zong Han sent him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The generals captured Yelü Mage, and Zong Han sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔以馬七百匹給宗翰軍，以田種千石、米七千石賑新附之民。

translations.literal: An edict granted seven hundred horses to Zong Han's army and used a thousand piculs of seed grain and seven thousand piculs of rice to relieve the newly submitted people.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted seven hundred horses to Zong Han's army and allotted a thousand piculs of seed grain and seven thousand piculs of rice to relieve the newly submitted population.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「新附之民，比及農時，度地以居之。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "For the newly submitted people, before the farming season arrives, survey land and settle them upon it."
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "For the newly submitted people, before the farming season comes, survey land and settle them on it."

sentences.zh: 宗翰請分宗望、撻懶、石古乃精兵討諸部。

translations.literal: Zong Han requested that elite troops of Zong Wang, Tawan, and Shigu'nai be detached to subdue the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han asked that picked troops from Zong Wang, Tawan, and Shigu'nai be detached to subdue the various tribes.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「宗望軍不可分，別以精銳五千給之。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "Zong Wang's army cannot be divided; separately give him five thousand picked troops."
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Zong Wang's army cannot be split off; give him five thousand picked troops separately."

sentences.zh: 宗翰朝太祖陵，入見上，奏曰：「先皇帝時，山西、南京諸部漢官，軍帥皆得承制除授。

translations.literal: Zong Han paid homage at the Taizu's tomb, entered to see the sovereign, and memorialized: "In the former emperor's time, Han officials of the Shanxi and Nanjing departments and military commanders could all appoint and dismiss on their own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han paid homage at the Taizu's tomb, entered audience, and memorialized: "Under the late emperor, Han officials in the Shanxi and Nanjing regions and army commanders were all allowed to appoint and dismiss on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 今南京皆循舊制，惟山西優以朝命。」

translations.literal: Now Nanjing all follows the old system; only Shanxi is favored with court appointments."
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing still follows the old practice, but in Shanxi appointments now come only from court."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「一用先皇帝燕京所降詔敕從事，卿等度其勤力而遷授之。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "Use entirely the edicts and orders issued when the former emperor reduced Yanjing, and you, sirs, should assess their diligence and promote and appoint them accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered: "Follow entirely the edicts issued when the late emperor took Yanjing, and promote and appoint men according to their merit."

sentences.zh: 宗翰複奏曰：「先皇帝征遼之初，圖宋協力夾攻，故許以燕地。

translations.literal: Zong Han again memorialized: "When the former emperor first campaigned against Liao, he planned for Song cooperation in a pincer attack, and therefore promised them the Yan region.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han memorialized again: "When the late emperor first marched against Liao, he hoped the Song would join in a coordinated attack, and therefore promised them the Yan region.

sentences.zh: 宋人既盟之後，請加幣以求山西諸鎮，先皇帝辭其加幣。

translations.literal: After the Song had made the alliance, they asked to increase the tribute to obtain the Shanxi garrisons; the former emperor refused the added tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song had sworn the alliance, they offered more tribute to obtain the Shanxi garrisons, but the late emperor refused the added payment.

sentences.zh: 盟書曰：'無容匿逋逃，誘擾邊民。

translations.literal: The alliance document said: 'You shall not harbor fugitives or entice and harass border people.'
translations.idiomatic: The treaty read: "You shall not harbor fugitives or entice and harass our border people."

sentences.zh: ' 今宋數路招納叛亡，厚以恩賞。

translations.literal: Now the Song on several routes recruit and accept defectors and rebels, rewarding them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now the Song on several routes recruit defectors and rebels and reward them generously.

sentences.zh: 累疏叛人姓名，索之童貫，嘗期以月日，約以哲書，一無所至。

translations.literal: We repeatedly listed the names of rebels and demanded them from Tong Guan, setting dates by month and day and pledging in solemn documents, yet nothing was ever delivered.
translations.idiomatic: We have repeatedly sent lists of defectors and demanded their return from Tong Guan, setting deadlines month by month and binding him with solemn pledges, yet not one man has been handed over.

sentences.zh: 盟未期年，今已如此，萬世守約，其可望乎。

translations.literal: The alliance is not yet a full year old, and already it is like this; can we hope they will keep the pact for ten thousand generations?
translations.idiomatic: The alliance is not yet a year old and already they behave like this—how can we expect them to keep faith for ages to come?

sentences.zh: 且西鄙未甯，割付山西諸郡，則諸軍失屯據之所，將有經略，或難持久，請姑置勿割。」

translations.literal: Moreover the western frontier is not yet settled. If we cede the Shanxi prefectures, the armies will lose their garrison positions; when we undertake further operations, it may be hard to endure. I ask that for the present we set aside the cession."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the western frontier is not yet secure. If we hand over the Shanxi prefectures, our armies lose their garrison bases; when we campaign again we may not be able to hold the ground. I ask that for now we set the cession aside."

sentences.zh: 上悉如所請。

translations.literal: The sovereign approved all as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved everything he had asked.

sentences.zh: 上以宗翰破遼，經略夏國奉表稱籓，深嘉其功，以馬十匹，使宗翰自擇二匹，余賜群帥。

translations.literal: Because Zong Han had defeated Liao and secured the Western Xia's submission with a memorial of vassalage, the sovereign greatly praised his merit. He granted ten horses, letting Zong Han choose two for himself and giving the rest to the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zong Han had broken Liao and brought the Western Xia to submit as a vassal, the emperor greatly praised his service. He granted ten horses, let Zong Han choose two for himself, and gave the rest to the commanders.

sentences.zh: 及斡魯奏宋不遣歲幣戶口事，且將渝盟，不可不備。

translations.literal: When Wolu memorialized that the Song had not sent the annual tribute and household registers and were about to break the alliance, preparations could not be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: When Wolu reported that the Song had failed to deliver the annual tribute and household registers and were about to break the alliance, the court could not neglect its defenses.

sentences.zh: 太宗命宗翰取諸路戶籍按籍索之。

translations.literal: The Taizong ordered Zong Han to take household registers from all routes and demand them according to the registers.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong ordered Zong Han to take household registers from every route and demand delivery according to the rolls.

sentences.zh: 而闍母再奏宋敗盟有狀，宗翰、宗望俱請伐宋。

translations.literal: Then Chanmu again memorialized that the Song's breach of the alliance was proven; Zong Han and Zong Wang both requested an attack on Song.
translations.idiomatic: Then Chanmu again reported clear proof that the Song had broken the treaty, and both Zong Han and Zong Wang asked to attack Song.

sentences.zh: 於是，諳班勃極烈杲領都元帥，居京師，宗翰為左副元帥，自太原路代宋。

translations.literal: Thereupon Anban Bojilie Gao took the post of supreme commander and remained in the capital; Zong Han was left deputy commander and was to replace Song from the Taiyuan route.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Anban Bojilie Gao became supreme commander and remained in the capital; Zong Han was made left deputy commander and was to invade Song from the Taiyuan route.

sentences.zh: 宗翰發自河陰，遂降朔州，克代州，圍太原府。

translations.literal: Zong Han set out from Heyin, then reduced Shuozhou, took Daizhou, and besieged Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han set out from Heyin, reduced Shuozhou, took Daizhou, and besieged Taiyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋河東、陝西軍四萬救太原，敗於汾河之北，殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: Song forces from Hedong and Shaanxi, forty thousand strong, came to relieve Taiyuan and were defeated north of the Fen River; more than ten thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Forty thousand Song troops from Hedong and Shaanxi marched to relieve Taiyuan and were defeated north of the Fen River; more than ten thousand were slain.

sentences.zh: 宗望自河北趨汴，久不聞問，遂留銀術可等圍太原，宗翰率師而南。

translations.literal: Zong Wang hastened toward Bian from Hebei; for a long time there was no word, so Zong Han left Yinchuoke and others to besiege Taiyuan and led the army south.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang had hurried toward Bian from Hebei, but for a long time no word came from him, so Zong Han left Yinchuoke and others to continue the siege of Taiyuan and marched south with the main army.

sentences.zh: 天會四年降定諸縣及威勝軍，下隆德府實潞州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianhui he reduced and settled the various counties and Weisheng Army, and took Longde Prefecture, which was Luzhou in fact.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 4 he reduced the surrounding counties and Weisheng Army and took Longde Prefecture, the true seat of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 軍至澤州，宋使至軍中，始知割三鎮講和事。

translations.literal: When the army reached Ze Prefecture, Song envoys came to the camp, and only then did they learn of the peace by ceding the three garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Ze Prefecture, Song envoys arrived in camp and they learned for the first time of the peace settlement involving the cession of the three garrisons.

sentences.zh: 路允迪以宋割太原詔書來，太原人不受詔。

translations.literal: Lu Yundi came with the Song edict ceding Taiyuan, but the people of Taiyuan would not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yundi brought the Song edict ceding Taiyuan, but the people of Taiyuan refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 宗翰取文水及盂縣，複留銀術可圍太原。

translations.literal: Zong Han took Wenshui and Yu County, again leaving Yinchuoke to besiege Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han took Wenshui and Yu County and again left Yinchuoke to continue the siege of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 宗翰乃還山西。

translations.literal: Zong Han then returned to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han then withdrew to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 宋少帝誘蕭仲恭貽書餘睹，以興複遼社稷以動之。

translations.literal: The Song Lesser Emperor induced Xiao Zhonggong to send a letter to Yudu, moving him with the prospect of restoring the Liao state.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Lesser Emperor induced Xiao Zhonggong to write to Yudu, urging him with the promise of restoring the Liao dynasty.

sentences.zh: 蕭仲恭獻其書，詔複伐宋。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhonggong presented the letter, and an edict ordered another campaign against Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhonggong presented the letter, and an edict ordered another attack on Song.

sentences.zh: 八月，宗翰發自西京。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Zong Han set out from Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zong Han set out from Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 九月丙寅，宗翰克太原，執宋經略使張孝純等。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day of the ninth month Zong Han took Taiyuan and seized Song frontier commissioner Zhang Xiaochun and others.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in the ninth month Zong Han took Taiyuan and seized the Song frontier commissioner Zhang Xiaochun and others.

sentences.zh: 鶻沙虎取平遙，降靈石、介休、孝義諸縣。

translations.literal: Hushahu took Pingyao and reduced Lingshi, Jiexiu, Xiaoyi, and the other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Hushahu took Pingyao and reduced Lingshi, Jiexiu, Xiaoyi, and the other counties.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲子，宗翰自太原趨汴，降威勝軍，克隆德府，遂取澤州。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day of the eleventh month Zong Han hastened from Taiyuan toward Bian, reduced Weisheng Army, took Longde Prefecture, and then took Ze Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi in the eleventh month Zong Han marched from Taiyuan toward Bian, reduced Weisheng Army, took Longde Prefecture, and then seized Ze Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 撒刺荅等先已破天井關，進逼河陽，破宋兵萬人，降其城。

translations.literal: Salada and others had already broken Tianjing Pass, pressed on toward Heyang, defeated ten thousand Song troops, and reduced the city.
translations.idiomatic: Salada and others had already forced Tianjing Pass, pressed on to Heyang, routed ten thousand Song troops, and reduced the city.

sentences.zh: 宗翰攻懷州，克之。

translations.literal: Zong Han attacked Huai Prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han attacked Huai Prefecture and took it.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，渡河。

translations.literal: On the dinghai day he crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 閏月，宗翰至汴，與宗望會兵。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month Zong Han reached Bian and joined forces with Zong Wang.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Zong Han reached Bian and joined Zong Wang.

sentences.zh: 宋約畫河為界，複請修好。

translations.literal: The Song proposed drawing the river as the boundary and again asked to restore friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: The Song proposed the river as the boundary and again asked for peace.

sentences.zh: 不克和。

translations.literal: Peace could not be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: No agreement could be reached.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，銀術可等克汴州。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day Yinchuoke and others took Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Yinchuoke and others took Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，宋少帝詣軍前，舍青城。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day the Song Lesser Emperor came before the army and lodged at Qingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the Song Lesser Emperor came before the army and lodged at Qingcheng.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸亥，少帝奏表降。

translations.literal: On the guihai day of the twelfth month the Lesser Emperor submitted a memorial of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai in the twelfth month the Lesser Emperor submitted his surrender memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔元帥府曰：「將帥士卒立功者，第其功之高下遷賞之。

translations.literal: An edict to the commander-in-chief's headquarters said: "For commanders, troops, and soldiers who have achieved merit, rank their achievements high and low and promote and reward them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the commander-in-chief's headquarters read: "For commanders and soldiers who have won merit, rank their achievements and promote and reward them accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其殞身行陣，沒于王事者，厚恤其家，賜贈官爵務從優厚。」

translations.literal: Those who died in the battle line in service to the state—generously relieve their families and grant posthumous offices and titles, striving for exceptional generosity."
translations.idiomatic: Those who fell in battle in the service of the state—relieve their families generously and grant posthumous offices and titles as richly as possible."

sentences.zh: 使勖就軍中勞賜宗翰、宗望，使皆執其手以勞之。

translations.literal: He sent Xu to the army to console and reward Zong Han and Zong Wang, and had him take each by the hand in consolation.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xu to the army to console and reward Zong Han and Zong Wang, bidding him take each by the hand in person.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，以宋二主及其宗族四百七十餘人及珪璋、寶印、袞冕、車輅、祭器、大樂、靈台、圖書，與大軍北還。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, with the two Song rulers and more than four hundred seventy of their clansmen, together with jade scepters and seals, robes and caps, carriages, ritual vessels, great music, observatories, and books, they returned north with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 5 they marched north with the main army, taking the two Song emperors and more than four hundred seventy members of their clan, along with jade regalia, imperial seals, robes and caps, carriages, ritual vessels, the great music, observatory instruments, and the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 七月，賜宗翰鐵券，除反逆外，餘皆不問，賜與甚厚。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he granted Zong Han an iron certificate: except for rebellion and treason, nothing else would be held against him, and the gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he granted Zong Han an iron certificate of mercy—except for rebellion and treason, no offense would be held against him—and showered him with rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 宗翰奏河北、河東府鎮州縣請擇前資官良能者任之，以安新民。

translations.literal: Zong Han memorialized that for the prefectures, garrisons, and counties of Hebei and Hedong, former officials of proven ability should be chosen to hold office so as to settle the newly submitted people.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han memorialized that for the prefectures, garrisons, and counties of Hebei and Hedong, proven former officials of ability should be appointed to pacify the newly submitted population.

sentences.zh: 上遣耶律暉等從宗翰行。

translations.literal: The sovereign sent Yelü Hui and others to accompany Zong Han on his march.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yelü Hui and others to accompany Zong Han.

sentences.zh: 詔黃龍府路、南路、東京路於所部各選如耶律暉者遣之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Huanglongfu, Southern, and Eastern Capital routes each to select men like Yelü Hui from their jurisdictions and send them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Huanglongfu, Southern, and Eastern Capital routes each to choose men of Yelü Hui's caliber from their jurisdictions and dispatch them.

sentences.zh: 宗翰遂趨洛陽。

translations.literal: Zong Han then hastened toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han then marched on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 宋董植以兵至鄭州，鄭州人複叛。

translations.literal: The Song officer Dong Zhi came with troops to Zheng Prefecture, and the people of Zheng rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Dong Zhi marched on Zheng Prefecture with troops, and the people of Zheng rose in revolt again.

sentences.zh: 宗翰使諸將擊董植軍，複取鄭州。

translations.literal: Zong Han ordered the generals to strike Dong Zhi's army and again took Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han sent his generals against Dong Zhi's force and recovered Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遂遷洛陽、襄陽、潁昌、汝、鄭、均、房、唐、鄧、陳、蔡之民于河北，而遣婁室平陝西州郡。

translations.literal: He then moved the people of Luoyang, Xiangyang, Yingchang, Ru, Zheng, Jun, Fang, Tang, Deng, Chen, and Cai to Hebei, and sent Wushi to pacify the prefectures and counties of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He then relocated the populations of Luoyang, Xiangyang, Yingchang, Ru, Zheng, Jun, Fang, Tang, Deng, Chen, and Cai to Hebei, and sent Wushi to pacify the prefectures and counties of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 是時河東寇盜尚多，宗翰乃分留將士，夾河屯守，而還師山西。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and robbers were still numerous in Hedong, so Zong Han left troops stationed on both banks of the river and returned the army to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were still numerous in Hedong at the time, so Zong Han left detachments garrisoned on both banks of the river and withdrew the main army to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 昏德公致書「請立趙氏，奉職修貢，民心必喜，萬世利也。」

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor sent a letter: "I ask that the Zhao house be established, that they hold office and pay tribute; the people's hearts will surely rejoice, and it will profit ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor wrote: "I ask that the Zhao house be restored to rule, that they hold office and pay tribute—the people will surely rejoice, and the benefit will last for ages."

sentences.zh: 宗翰受其書而不答。

translations.literal: Zong Han received the letter but did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han received the letter but made no reply.

sentences.zh: 康王遣王師正奉表，密以書招誘契彤、漢人。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kang sent Wang Shizheng to present a memorial, secretly using letters to entice and recruit Jurchens and Han people.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kang sent Wang Shizheng with a memorial and secretly used letters to recruit Jurchens and Han subjects.

sentences.zh: 獲其書奏之。

translations.literal: The letters were captured and presented in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The letters were seized and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗下詔伐康王。

translations.literal: The Taizong issued an edict to campaign against the Prince of Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong issued an edict ordering war against the Prince of Kang.

sentences.zh: 河北諸將欲罷陝西兵，並力南伐。

translations.literal: The Hebei generals wished to withdraw the Shaanxi troops and combine strength for a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Hebei commanders wanted to pull the Shaanxi armies back and concentrate everything on the southern advance.

sentences.zh: 河東諸將不可，曰：「陝西與西夏為鄰，事重體大，兵不可罷。」

translations.literal: The Hedong generals would not agree, saying: "Shaanxi borders the Western Xia; the matter is weighty and the stake is great—the troops cannot be withdrawn."
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong commanders objected: "Shaanxi borders the Western Xia; the stakes are too high to pull those troops back."

sentences.zh: 宗翰曰：「初與夏約夾攻宋人，而夏人弗應。

translations.literal: Zong Han said: "At first we agreed with Xia on a pincer attack against the Song, but the Xia did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han said, "We first agreed with Xia on a coordinated attack on Song, but they never answered.

sentences.zh: 而耶律大石在西北，交通西夏。

translations.literal: Yet Yelü Dashi is in the northwest, in communication with the Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yelü Dashi is in the northwest, in contact with the Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 吾舍陝西而會師河北，彼必謂我有急難。

translations.literal: If we abandon Shaanxi and concentrate the armies in Hebei, they will surely think we are in urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: If we abandon Shaanxi and mass our armies in Hebei, they will surely think we are in desperate straits.

sentences.zh: 河北不足虞，宜先事陝西，略定五路，既弱西夏，然後取宋。」

translations.literal: Hebei is not worth worrying over; we should first attend to Shaanxi, secure the five routes, weaken the Western Xia, and then take Song."
translations.idiomatic: Hebei is not what we need to fear. We should secure Shaanxi first, bring the five routes under control, weaken the Western Xia, and only then take Song."

sentences.zh: 宗翰蓋有意于夏人也。

translations.literal: Zong Han probably had designs on the Xia people.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han clearly had designs on the Western Xia as well.

sentences.zh: 議久不決，奏請於上，上曰：「康王構當窮其所往而追之。

translations.literal: Deliberation long remained unresolved; they memorialized the sovereign, who said: "Zhao Gou must be pursued to the end of wherever he flees.
translations.idiomatic: Debate dragged on without resolution until they appealed to the emperor, who said, "Zhao Gou must be pursued wherever he flees.

sentences.zh: 俟平宋，當立籓輔如張邦昌者。

translations.literal: When Song is pacified, a vassal ruler like Zhang Bangchang should be established.
translations.idiomatic: When Song is pacified, we should set up a vassal ruler like Zhang Bangchang.

sentences.zh: 陝右之地，亦未可置而不取。」

translations.literal: The lands of Shaanxi west also cannot be set aside and left untaken."
translations.idiomatic: The lands west of the passes cannot be left untaken either."

sentences.zh: 於是婁室、蒲察帥師，繩果、婆盧火監戰，平陝西。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wushi and Pucha led the armies; Shengguo and Poluhuo supervised the fighting; and Shaanxi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wushi and Pucha led the armies, with Shengguo and Poluhuo overseeing operations, and Shaanxi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 銀術可守太原，耶律餘睹留西京。

translations.literal: Yinchuoke guarded Taiyuan; Yelü Yudu remained at Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yinchuoke garrisoned Taiyuan and Yelü Yudu remained at Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 宗翰會東軍于黎陽津，遂會睿宗於濮。

translations.literal: Zong Han joined the eastern army at Liyang Ford and then met the Ruizong at Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han joined the eastern army at Liyang Ford and then met the Ruizong at Pu.

sentences.zh: 進兵至東平，宋知府權邦彥棄家宵遁，降其城，駐軍東平東南五十里。

translations.literal: Advancing to Dongping, the Song prefect Quan Bangyan abandoned his household and fled by night; they reduced the city and encamped fifty li southeast of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced to Dongping. The Song prefect Quan Bangyan abandoned his family and fled by night; the city submitted, and the army encamped fifty li southeast of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 複取徐州。

translations.literal: They again took Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They then took Xuzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 先是，宋人運江、淮金幣皆在徐州官庫，盡得之，分給諸軍。

translations.literal: Earlier the Song had transported gold and tribute from the Yangzi and Huai stored in the Xuzhou government treasury; all was obtained and distributed to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Song had shipped gold and tribute from the Yangzi and Huai regions to the Xuzhou government treasury; the Jin seized it all and distributed it among the armies.

sentences.zh: 襲慶府來降。

translations.literal: Xiqing Prefecture came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiqing Prefecture submitted.

sentences.zh: 宋知濟南府劉豫以城降於撻懶。

translations.literal: The Song prefect of Jinan, Liu Yu, surrendered the city to Tawan.
translations.idiomatic: The Song prefect of Jinan, Liu Yu, surrendered the city to Tawan.

sentences.zh: 乃遣拔離速、烏林荅泰欲、馬五襲康王於揚州，未至百五十里，馬五以五百騎先馳至揚州城下。

translations.literal: They then sent Balisu, Wulindá Taiyu, and Ma Wu to strike the Prince of Kang at Yangzhou. Before they had gone one hundred fifty li, Ma Wu with five hundred horsemen galloped ahead to below Yangzhou's walls.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Balisu, Wulindá Taiyu, and Ma Wu to strike at the Prince of Kang at Yangzhou. Before the main force had covered one hundred fifty li, Ma Wu galloped ahead with five hundred horsemen to the walls of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 康王聞兵來，已於前一夕渡江矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kang, hearing troops were coming, had already crossed the river the night before.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kang, hearing that troops were coming, had already crossed the river the night before.

sentences.zh: 於是，康王以書請存趙氏社稷。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Kang by letter asked that the Zhao ancestral temple and altars be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kang then wrote asking that the Zhao dynasty be allowed to survive.

sentences.zh: 先是，康王嘗致書元帥府，稱「大宋皇帝構致書大金元帥帳前」，至是乃貶去大號，自稱「宋康王趙構謹致書元帥閤下」。

translations.literal: Earlier the Prince of Kang had sent a letter to the commander-in-chief's headquarters styled "The Great Song Emperor Gou respectfully addresses the Great Jin commander-in-chief's tent." Now he demoted his grand title and styled himself "The Song Prince of Kang Zhao Gou respectfully addresses the commander-in-chief's pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Prince of Kang had written to the commander-in-chief's headquarters as "The Great Song Emperor Gou respectfully addresses the Great Jin commander-in-chief." Now he dropped the grand title and styled himself "The Song Prince of Kang Zhao Gou respectfully addresses the commander-in-chief's pavilion."

sentences.zh: 其四月、七月兩書皆然。

translations.literal: His letters of the fourth and seventh months were both like this.
translations.idiomatic: His letters of the fourth and seventh months both followed this form.

sentences.zh: 元帥府答其書，招之使降。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief's headquarters answered his letter, summoning him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The commander-in-chief's headquarters answered, summoning him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 於是，撻懶、宗弼、拔離速、馬五等分道南伐。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tawan, Zong Bi, Balisu, Ma Wu, and others campaigned south by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Tawan, Zong Bi, Balisu, Ma Wu, and others marched south by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 宗弼之軍渡江取建康，入於杭州。

translations.literal: Zong Bi's army crossed the river, took Jiankang, and entered Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Bi's army crossed the river, took Jiankang, and pushed on to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 康王入海，阿裏、蒲盧渾等自明州行海三百里，追之弗及。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kang went to sea; Ali, Puluhun, and others from Ming Prefecture sailed three hundred li on the sea but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kang put to sea. Ali, Puluhun, and others sailed three hundred li from Ming Prefecture but could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 宗弼乃還。

translations.literal: Zong Bi then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Bi then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其後宗翰欲用徐文策伐江南，睿宗、宗弼議不合，乃止。

translations.literal: Later Zong Han wished to use Xu Wen's plan to campaign against Jiangnan; the Ruizong and Zong Bi disagreed in counsel, and so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zong Han wanted to use Xu Wen's plan for a campaign against Jiangnan, but the Ruizong and Zong Bi could not agree, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 語在《劉豫傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Liu Yu."
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the "Biography of Liu Yu."

sentences.zh: 歸德叛，都統大糺裏平之。

translations.literal: Guide rebelled; Commander-in-Chief Da Qiuli pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Guide rebelled; Commander-in-Chief Da Qiuli put down the revolt.

sentences.zh: 孫秉德、斜哥。

translations.literal: Grandsons: Bingde, Xiege.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons: Bingde and Xiege.

sentences.zh: 秉德別有傳。

translations.literal: Bingde has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Bingde has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 子 斜哥

translations.literal: Son: Xiege
translations.idiomatic: Son: Xiege

sentences.zh: 斜哥，累官同知曷蘇館節度使事。

translations.literal: Xiege, through successive offices, became associate commissioner of the Yisu Hall Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Xiege rose through successive offices to become associate commissioner of the Yisu Hall Military Commission.

sentences.zh: 大定初，除刑部侍郎，充都統，與副統完顏布輝自東京先赴中都，輒署置官吏，私用官中財物。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he was appointed vice minister of justice and made commander-in-chief. With Deputy Commander Wanyan Buhui he went from the Eastern Capital ahead to the Central Capital, where they arbitrarily appointed and installed officials and privately used government property.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading era he was made vice minister of justice and commander-in-chief. With Deputy Commander Wanyan Buhui he went from the Eastern Capital ahead to the Central Capital, where they appointed officials on their own authority and misused government property.

sentences.zh: 世宗至中都，事覺，斜哥當死，布輝當除名。

translations.literal: When the Shizong reached the Central Capital the matter came to light; Xiege deserved death and Buhui deserved removal from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizong reached the Central Capital the affair came to light; by law Xiege deserved death and Buhui removal from office.

sentences.zh: 詔寬減，斜哥除名，布輝削兩階，解職。

translations.literal: An edict reduced the penalties: Xiege was removed from the rolls; Buhui was demoted two ranks and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reduced the penalties: Xiege was struck from the rolls and Buhui was demoted two ranks and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 二年，起為大宗正丞，除祁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled as director of the Great Clan Directorate and appointed prefect of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was recalled as director of the Great Clan Directorate and appointed prefect of Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐贓枉法，當死，詔杖一百五十，除名。

translations.literal: For corruption and perversion of the law he deserved death; an edict ordered one hundred fifty strokes of the staff and removal from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: For corruption and abuse of the law he deserved death; an edict ordered one hundred fifty strokes of the staff and struck him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 遣左衛將軍夾谷查刺諭斜哥曰：「卿何面目至鄉中與宗族相見。

translations.literal: The Left Guard General Jiagu Zhaci was sent to instruct Xiege: "With what face can you go home and meet your clan and kin?
translations.idiomatic: The Left Guard General Jiagu Zhaci was sent to tell Xiege, "With what face can you go home and face your clan?

sentences.zh: 今徙鄜州，以家人自隨，俟汝身死，聽家人從便。」

translations.literal: Now you are exiled to Fu Prefecture; take your household with you. When you die, your family may do as they please."
translations.idiomatic: You are now exiled to Fu Prefecture with your household. When you die, your family may go where they choose."

sentences.zh: 久之，起同知興中尹，遷唐括部族節度使，曆開遠、順義軍。

translations.literal: After a long while he was recalled as associate prefect of Xingzhong and transferred to Tangguo Tribal Military Commissioner, serving successively at Kaiyuan and Shunyi Armies.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled as associate prefect of Xingzhong, then made Tangguo Tribal Military Commissioner, and later served at Kaiyuan and Shunyi Armies.

sentences.zh: 斜哥前在雲內受贓，禦史台劾奏，上謂宰臣曰：「斜哥今三犯矣，蓋其資質鄙惡如此。」

translations.literal: Xiege had earlier accepted bribes at Yunnei; the Censorate impeached him, and the sovereign said to the chief ministers: "Xiege has now offended three times; his nature is base and vile in just this way."
translations.idiomatic: Xiege had earlier taken bribes at Yunnei; the Censorate impeached him, and the emperor told his chief ministers, "Xiege has now offended three times—his nature is as base as this."

sentences.zh: 令強幹吏鞫之。

translations.literal: He ordered capable and forceful officials to interrogate the case.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered capable officers to investigate the case thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 獄成，法當死。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, by law he deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded, the law called for death.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「斜哥祖父秦王宗翰有大功，特免死，杖一百五十，除名。」

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "Xiege's grandfather the Prince of Qin, Zong Han, rendered great service; specially exempt him from death, order one hundred fifty strokes of the staff, and remove him from the rolls."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Xiege's grandfather the Prince of Qin, Zong Han, rendered great service. Spare his life, order one hundred fifty strokes of the staff, and strike him from the rolls."

sentences.zh: 久之，複起為勸農副使。

translations.literal: After a long while he was again recalled as vice commissioner for encouraging agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again recalled as vice commissioner for encouraging agriculture.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宗翰內能謀國，外能謀敵，決策制勝，有古名將之風。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Zong Han could plan for the state within and plot against enemies without; in deciding policy and securing victory he had the manner of the famous generals of old.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Zong Han could plan for the state at home and plot against enemies abroad; in deciding strategy and securing victory he had the manner of the great generals of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 臨潢既捷，諸將皆有怠忽之心，而請伐不已。

translations.literal: After victory at Linhuang the generals all grew slack and neglectful, yet he never ceased requesting campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Linhuang the other generals grew slack, yet he never stopped urging further campaigns.

sentences.zh: 越千里以襲遼主，諸將皆有畏顧之心，而請期不已。

translations.literal: Crossing a thousand li to strike the Liao ruler, the generals all had hearts of fear and hesitation, yet he never ceased pressing for the date of advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the army had to cross a thousand li to strike the Liao emperor, the other generals shrank back in fear, yet he never stopped pressing for the day of battle.

sentences.zh: 觀其欲置江、淮，專事陝服，當時無有能識其意者。

translations.literal: Observing that he wished to set aside the Yangzi and Huai and devote himself to securing Shaanxi, at the time there was no one who could understand his intent.
translations.idiomatic: When one sees that he meant to set aside the Yangzi and Huai and concentrate on securing the western passes, no one at the time understood what he was after.

sentences.zh: 甫釋干戈，斂衽歸朝，以定熙宗之位，精誠之發，孰可掩哉。

translations.literal: Hardly had he laid down arms when he straightened his robe and returned to court to settle the position of the Xizong—such an outpouring of loyalty, who could conceal it?
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he laid down his arms when he straightened his robes and returned to court to secure the Xizong's succession—such devotion, who could hide it?

sentences.zh: 宗望本名斡魯補，又作斡離不，太祖第二子也。

translations.literal: Zong Wang's original name was Wolubu, also written Wo Libu; he was the Taizu's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang's original name was Wolubu, also written Wo Libu; he was the Taizu's second son.

sentences.zh: 每從太祖征伐，常在左右。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed the Taizu on campaign he was constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign with the Taizu he was constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 都統杲已克中京，宗翰在北安州，獲遼護衛習泥烈，知遼主在鴛鴦濼，宗翰請襲之。

translations.literal: Commander Gao had already taken Central Capital. Zong Han was at Bei'an Prefecture and captured the Liao guard Xinilie, learning that the Liao ruler was at Yuanyang Marsh; Zong Han requested a strike against him.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Gao had already taken Central Capital. Zong Han was at Bei'an Prefecture when he captured the Liao guard Xinilie and learned that the Liao emperor was at Yuanyang Marsh; Zong Han asked to strike at him.

sentences.zh: 杲出青嶺，遼兵三百餘掠降人家貲。

translations.literal: Gao came out by Qing Ridge; more than three hundred Liao troops were plundering the goods of submitted households.
translations.idiomatic: Gao marched out through Qing Ridge, where more than three hundred Liao troops were plundering submitted households.

sentences.zh: 宗望曰：「若生致此輩，可審得遼主所在虛實。」

translations.literal: Zong Wang said: "If we take these men alive, we can ascertain the truth of where the Liao ruler is."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang said, "If we take these men alive, we can learn exactly where the Liao emperor is."

sentences.zh: 遂與宗弼率百騎進。

translations.literal: He then advanced with Zong Bi at the head of a hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: He then advanced with Zong Bi at the head of a hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 騎多罷乏，獨與馬和尚逐越盧、孛古、野裏斯等，留一騎趣後軍，即馳擊敗之，生擒五人。

translations.literal: Many of the horses were exhausted and worn; he alone with Monk Ma pursued Yuelu, Liguo, Yelisi, and others, leaving one horseman to hurry to the rear army, then galloped to attack and defeat them, taking five men alive.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the horses were spent; he alone with Monk Ma pursued Yuelu, Liguo, Yelisi, and others, leaving one rider to summon the rear guard, then charged and routed them, taking five men alive.

sentences.zh: 因審遼主尚在鴛鴦濼未去無疑也。

translations.literal: Thus they verified that the Liao ruler was still at Yuanyang Marsh and had not yet left—there was no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: They thus confirmed beyond doubt that the Liao emperor was still at Yuanyang Marsh and had not yet fled.

sentences.zh: 於是進兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon they advanced the army.
translations.idiomatic: The army then marched forward.

sentences.zh: 宗翰倍道兼行，追遼主于五院司，不及。

translations.literal: Zong Han doubled his march and pursued the Liao ruler to the Five Yuan Office but did not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han forced the march and pursued the Liao emperor to the Five Yuan Office but could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 婁室等追之至白水濼，遼主走陰山。

translations.literal: Wushi and others pursued him to Baishui Marsh; the Liao ruler fled to Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wushi and others pursued him to Baishui Marsh; the Liao emperor fled toward Yinshan.

sentences.zh: 遼秦晉國王捏裏自立於燕京。

translations.literal: The Liao Prince of Qin and Jin, Nieli, declared himself ruler at Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao Prince of Qin and Jin, Nieli, declared himself ruler at Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 新降州部，人心不固，杲使宗望請太祖臨軍。

translations.literal: In the newly submitted prefectures and districts hearts were not firm; Gao had Zong Wang request that the Taizu come to the army in person.
translations.idiomatic: The newly submitted prefectures were still unsettled; Gao had Zong Wang ask the Taizu to come to the army in person.

sentences.zh: 宗望至京師，百官入賀。

translations.literal: Zong Wang reached the capital; the hundred officials entered to congratulate him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Wang reached the capital, the officials came to congratulate him.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「宗望與十餘騎經涉兵寇數千里，可嘉也。」

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "Zong Wang with a little more than ten horsemen passed through enemy troops for several thousand li—this is praiseworthy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zong Wang with little more than a dozen horsemen passed through enemy country for thousands of li—that is worthy of praise."

sentences.zh: 上宴群臣，歡甚，宗望奏曰：「今雲中新定，諸路遼兵尚數萬，遼主尚在陰山、天德之間，而捏裏自立於燕京，新降之民，其心未固，是以諸將望陛下幸軍中也。」

translations.literal: The sovereign feasted the ministers with great joy. Zong Wang memorialized: "Now Yunzhong is newly settled, yet Liao troops on the various routes still number in the tens of thousands. The Liao ruler is still between Yinshan and Tiande, while Nieli has declared himself at Yanjing. The hearts of the newly submitted people are not yet firm; therefore the generals hope Your Majesty will come to the army in person."
translations.idiomatic: At a feast for his ministers the emperor was in high spirits. Zong Wang memorialized: "Yunzhong is newly pacified, yet Liao forces on every route still number in the tens of thousands. The Liao emperor is still between Yinshan and Tiande, while Nieli has declared himself at Yanjing. The newly submitted people are not yet loyal. That is why the generals hope Your Majesty will come to the army in person."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「懸軍遠伐，授以成算，豈能盡合機事。

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "When an army is sent far on campaign, the plans given in advance cannot match every turn of events.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "When an army campaigns far from home, the plans drawn up in advance cannot match every turn of events.

sentences.zh: 朕以六月朔啟行。」

translations.literal: I shall set out on the first day of the sixth month."
translations.idiomatic: I shall set out on the first day of the sixth month."

sentences.zh: 既次大濼西南，果使希尹奏請徙西南招討司諸部於內地。

translations.literal: After halting southwest of Great Marsh, Gao had Xiyin memorialize requesting that the tribes of the Southwest Pacification Commission be moved into the interior.
translations.idiomatic: After encamping southwest of Great Marsh, Gao had Xiyin memorialize asking that the tribes of the Southwest Pacification Commission be moved into the interior.

sentences.zh: 上顧謂群臣曰：「徙諸部人當出何路？」

translations.literal: The sovereign turned and asked the ministers: "By what route should the people of the various tribes be moved?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his ministers and asked, "By what route should these tribes be moved?"

sentences.zh: 宗望對曰：「中京殘弊，芻糧不給，由上京為宜。

translations.literal: Zong Wang answered: "Central Capital is ruined and depleted; fodder and grain cannot be supplied. It would be fitting to go by the Upper Capital route.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang answered, "Central Capital is ruined and cannot supply fodder or grain. The Upper Capital route would be better.

sentences.zh: 然新降之人，遽爾騷動，未降者必皆疑懼。

translations.literal: Yet if the newly submitted people are suddenly stirred into unrest, those not yet submitted will surely all grow suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: But if we suddenly stir up the newly submitted, those not yet submitted will surely grow suspicious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 勞師害人，所失多矣。」

translations.literal: To weary the army and harm the people—what is lost will be great."
translations.idiomatic: We would weary the army and harm the people—the losses would outweigh the gain."

sentences.zh: 上京謂臨潢府也。

translations.literal: Upper Capital means Linhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Upper Capital means Linhuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上乃下其議，命軍帥度宜行之。

translations.literal: The sovereign then set aside the proposal and ordered the army commanders to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then set the proposal aside and ordered the commanders to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 上聞遼主在大魚濼，自將精兵萬人襲之。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Liao ruler was at Great Fish Marsh, the sovereign personally led ten thousand elite troops to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Liao emperor was at Great Fish Marsh, the emperor personally led ten thousand elite troops to strike him.

sentences.zh: 蒲家奴、宗望率兵四千為前鋒，晝夜兼行，馬多乏，追及遼主于石輦驛，軍士至者才千人，遼軍余二萬五千。

translations.literal: Pujianu and Zong Wang led four thousand troops as vanguard, marching day and night; many horses were exhausted. They overtook the Liao ruler at Shinian Post; soldiers who arrived numbered only a thousand, while Liao troops remaining were twenty-five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Pujianu and Zong Wang led four thousand men as vanguard, marching day and night until many horses were spent. They caught the Liao emperor at Shinian Post with only a thousand men at hand against more than twenty-five thousand Liao troops.

sentences.zh: 方治營壘，蒲家奴與諸將議。

translations.literal: Just as they were building camp fortifications, Pujianu deliberated with the generals.
translations.idiomatic: While they were still building camp defenses, Pujianu consulted the other generals.

sentences.zh: 餘睹曰：「我軍未集，人馬疲劇，未可戰。」

translations.literal: Yudu said: "Our army is not yet gathered; men and horses are worn and exhausted—we cannot fight."
translations.idiomatic: Yudu said, "Our army is not yet assembled and men and horses are exhausted—we cannot fight."

sentences.zh: 宗望曰：「今追及遼主而不亟戰，日入而遁，則無及。」

translations.literal: Zong Wang said: "Now that we have overtaken the Liao ruler, if we do not fight at once, when the sun sets he will escape and it will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang said, "We have caught the Liao emperor; if we do not fight at once, he will escape at sunset and we will never catch him."

sentences.zh: 遂戰，短兵接，遼兵圍之數重，士皆殊死戰。

translations.literal: They then fought at close quarters; Liao troops surrounded them in several rings, and the soldiers all fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: They gave battle at close quarters. Liao troops surrounded them in ring after ring, and the Jin soldiers fought as if each man meant to die.

sentences.zh: 遼主謂宗望兵少必敗，遂與嬪禦皆自高阜下平地觀戰。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler thought Zong Wang's few troops would surely be defeated, so with his consorts and attendants he all came down from the high mound to level ground to watch the battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor, thinking Zong Wang's small force was sure to lose, came down from a high mound with his consorts and attendants to watch the battle on level ground.

sentences.zh: 余睹示諸將曰：「此遼主麾蓋也。

translations.literal: Yudu showed the generals and said: "That is the Liao ruler's banner and canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Yudu pointed them out to the other generals: "That is the Liao emperor's banner and canopy.

sentences.zh: 若萃而薄之，可以得志。」

translations.literal: If we mass and press close upon it, we can achieve our aim."
translations.idiomatic: If we mass and press in on it, we can finish this."

sentences.zh: 騎兵馳赴之，遼主望見大驚，即遁去，遼兵遂潰。

translations.literal: The cavalry galloped toward it; the Liao ruler saw them and was greatly alarmed, immediately fled, and the Liao troops then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry charged toward it. The Liao emperor saw them, was terrified, and fled at once; the Liao army then broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 宗望等還。

translations.literal: Zong Wang and the others returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang and his party returned.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「遼主去不遠，亟追之。」

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "The Liao ruler is not far off—pursue him at once."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Liao emperor is not far off—pursue him at once."

sentences.zh: 宗望以騎兵千餘追之，蒲家奴為後繼。

translations.literal: Zong Wang with more than a thousand cavalry pursued him, Pujianu following as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang pursued with more than a thousand horsemen, Pujianu following as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 太祖已定燕京，斡魯為都統，宗望副之，襲遼主於陰山、青塚之間。

translations.literal: After the Taizu had settled Yanjing, Wolu served as commander-in-chief and Zong Wang as his deputy, striking at the Liao ruler between Yinshan and Green Tumulus.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu secured Yanjing, Wolu was made commander-in-chief with Zong Wang as his deputy, and they struck at the Liao emperor between Yinshan and Green Tumulus.

sentences.zh: 宗望、婁室、銀術可以三千軍分路襲之。

translations.literal: Zong Wang, Wushi, and Yinchuoke with three thousand troops struck him by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang, Wushi, and Yinchuoke took three thousand men and attacked by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 將至青塚，遇泥濘，眾不能進。

translations.literal: When they were about to reach Green Tumulus, they met mud and mire and the force could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: As they neared Green Tumulus they ran into mud and mire, and the army could not press on.

sentences.zh: 宗望與當海四騎以繩系遼都統林牙大石，使為鄉導，直至遼主營。

translations.literal: Zong Wang with Danghai and three other horsemen tied a rope to the Liao commander-in-chief Linya Dashi, made him serve as guide, and went straight to the Liao ruler's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang, Danghai, and three other riders bound the Liao commander Linya Dashi with ropes, forced him to guide them, and reached the Liao emperor's camp directly.

sentences.zh: 時遼主往應州，其嬪禦諸女見敵兵奄至驚駭欲奔，命騎下執之。

translations.literal: At the time the Liao ruler had gone toward Ying Prefecture; his consorts and various daughters, seeing enemy troops suddenly arrive, were alarmed and wished to flee; he ordered horsemen to dismount and seize them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor had gone toward Ying Prefecture. When his consorts and daughters saw enemy troops suddenly arrive, they panicked and tried to flee; he ordered his riders to dismount and seize them.

sentences.zh: 有頃，後軍至。

translations.literal: Before long the rear army arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the main force arrived.

sentences.zh: 遼太叔胡盧瓦妃，國王捏裏次妃，遼漢夫人，並其子秦王、許王，女骨欲、餘裏衍、斡裏衍、大奧野、次奧野、趙王妃斡裏衍，招討迪六，詳穩六斤，節度使孛迭、赤狗兒皆降。

translations.literal: The consort of the Liao Grand Uncle Hulüwa, the secondary consort of the state king Nieli, the Liao Han Lady, together with her sons the Princes of Qin and Xu, her daughters Guyü, Yuliyan, Woliyen, Eldest Aoye, Second Aoye, and the Princess of Zhao Woliyen, the pacification commissioner Dilü, the xianwen Liujin, and the military commissioners Bedie and Chigou'er all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The consort of the Liao Grand Uncle Hulüwa, the secondary consort of State King Nieli, Lady Han of Liao, her sons the Princes of Qin and Xu, her daughters Guyü, Yuliyan, Woliyen, Eldest Aoye, Second Aoye, and Princess of Zhao Woliyen, Pacification Commissioner Dilü, Xianwen Liujin, and Military Commissioners Bedie and Chigou'er all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 得車萬餘乘，惟梁王雅裏及其長女乘軍亂亡去。

translations.literal: They obtained more than ten thousand carts; only the Prince of Liang Yali and his eldest daughter escaped amid the army's disorder.
translations.idiomatic: They captured more than ten thousand carts. Only the Prince of Liang Yali and his eldest daughter slipped away in the confusion.

sentences.zh: 婁室、銀術可獲其左右輿帳。

translations.literal: Wushi and Yinchuoke captured his personal litters and tents.
translations.idiomatic: Wushi and Yinchuoke seized his personal carriages and tent encampment.

sentences.zh: 進至掃裏門，為書以招遼主。

translations.literal: Advancing to Saoli Gate, they wrote a letter to summon the Liao ruler.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to Saoli Gate and sent a written summons to the Liao emperor.

sentences.zh: 遼主自金城來，知其族屬皆見俘，率兵五千餘決戰。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler came from Jincheng; learning that all his clan and kin had been captured, he led more than five thousand troops to fight a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor came from Jincheng. Learning that his entire family had been taken captive, he led more than five thousand men to fight a decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 宗望以千兵擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zong Wang with a thousand troops defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang routed him with a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 遼主相去百步，遁去。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler was a hundred paces away and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor was barely a hundred paces away when he escaped.

sentences.zh: 獲其子趙王習泥烈及傳國璽。

translations.literal: They captured his son the Prince of Zhao Xinilie and the dynastic seal of transmission.
translations.idiomatic: They captured his son, the Prince of Zhao Xinilie, and the imperial seal of transmission.

sentences.zh: 追二十餘裏，盡得其從馬，而照裏、特末、胡巴魯、背荅別獲牧馬萬四千匹、車八千乘。

translations.literal: Pursuing for more than twenty li, they took all his accompanying horses; Zhaoli, Temo, Hubalu, and Beidabie obtained fourteen thousand pastured horses and eight thousand carts.
translations.idiomatic: After a pursuit of more than twenty li they seized all his attendant horses, while Zhaoli, Temo, Hubalu, and Beidabie captured fourteen thousand pastured horses and eight thousand carts.

sentences.zh: 及獻傳國璽於行在，太祖曰：「此群臣之功也。」

translations.literal: When the dynastic seal was presented at the mobile court, the Taizu said: "This is the merit of the ministers."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial seal was presented at the mobile court, the Taizu said, "This is the ministers' achievement."

sentences.zh: 遂置璽於懷中，東面恭謝天地，乃大錄諸帥功，加賞焉。

translations.literal: He then placed the seal in his bosom, bowed eastward in thanks to Heaven and Earth, and then recorded the achievements of the commanders at length and added rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He placed the seal against his breast, bowed eastward to Heaven and Earth in thanks, then took a full account of the commanders' achievements and rewarded them generously.

sentences.zh: 遼主乃使謀盧瓦持兔鈕金印請降。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler then sent Moulüwa bearing a gold seal with a rabbit knob to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao emperor then sent Moulüwa with a gold seal topped by a rabbit knob to sue for surrender.

sentences.zh: 宗望受之，視其文，乃「元帥燕國王之印」也。

translations.literal: Zong Wang received it and looked at its inscription—it read "Seal of the Grand Marshal, Prince of Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang accepted it and read the inscription: it was the "Seal of the Grand Marshal, Prince of Yan."

sentences.zh: 宗望複以書招之，諭以石晉北遷事。

translations.literal: Zong Wang again wrote to summon him, instructing him with the matter of the Later Jin's northward removal.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang wrote again to summon him, citing the precedent of the Later Jin's forced removal to the north.

sentences.zh: 遂使使諭夏國，示以和好，所以沮疑其救遼之心也。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to instruct the Xia state, showing goodwill—in order to discourage and shake their will to rescue Liao.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys to the Xia state offering friendship, hoping to weaken their resolve to aid the Liao.

sentences.zh: 宗望趨天德，遼耶律慎思降。

translations.literal: Zong Wang hastened toward Tiande; the Liao Yelü Shensi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang pressed toward Tiande, and the Liao general Yelü Shensi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 及候人吳十回，皆言夏國迎護遼主度大河矣。

translations.literal: When the scout Wu Shihui returned, all reported that the Xia state was escorting the Liao ruler across the Great River.
translations.idiomatic: When the scout Wu Shihui returned, all reported that the Xia were escorting the Liao emperor across the Great River.

sentences.zh: 宗望乃傳檄夏國曰：「果欲附我，當如前諭，執送遼主。

translations.literal: Zong Wang then issued a proclamation to the Xia state, saying: "If you truly wish to attach yourselves to us, you should, as previously instructed, seize and deliver the Liao ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang then sent a proclamation to the Xia: "If you truly mean to join us, do as we said before—seize the Liao emperor and hand him over.

sentences.zh: 若猶疑貳，恐有後悔。」

translations.literal: If you still waver in divided loyalty, I fear you will later regret it."
translations.idiomatic: If you still hedge your loyalty, you may come to regret it."

sentences.zh: 及遼秦王等以俘見太祖，太祖嘉宗望功，以遼蜀國公主余裏衍賜之。

translations.literal: When the Liao Prince of Qin and others were brought as captives before the Taizu, the Taizu praised Zong Wang's achievement and bestowed upon him the Liao Princess of Shu Yuliyan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao Prince of Qin and other captives were presented to the Taizu, the Taizu praised Zong Wang's achievement and gave him the Liao Princess of Shu, Yuliyan.

sentences.zh: 闍母與張覺戰，大敗於兔耳山。

translations.literal: Chanmu fought Zhang Jue and suffered a great defeat at Mount Tu'er.
translations.idiomatic: Chanmu fought Zhang Jue and was badly defeated at Mount Tu'er.

sentences.zh: 上使宗望問狀，就以闍母軍討張覺，降瀕海郡縣。

translations.literal: The sovereign had Zong Wang inquire into the situation, and then with Chanmu's army subdue Zhang Jue, bringing the coastal prefectures and counties to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zong Wang to investigate, then used Chanmu's army to campaign against Zhang Jue and brought the coastal prefectures and counties to submission.

sentences.zh: 遂與覺戰于南京城東。

translations.literal: He then fought Jue east of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then fought Zhang Jue east of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 覺敗，宵遁奔宋，語在《覺傳》。

translations.literal: Jue was defeated, fled by night to Song—the account is in the "Biography of Jue."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue was defeated and fled by night to Song; the full account appears in his biography.

sentences.zh: 城中人執覺父及其二子來獻，宗望殺之。

translations.literal: Men in the city seized Jue's father and his two sons and presented them; Zong Wang had them killed.
translations.idiomatic: City residents seized Zhang Jue's father and two sons and handed them over; Zong Wang had them executed.

sentences.zh: 使以詔書宣諭城中張敦固等出降。

translations.literal: He sent men with an edict to proclaim to Zhang Dun'gu and others in the city that they should come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an edict summoning Zhang Dun'gu and others in the city to surrender.

sentences.zh: 使使與敦固俱入城收兵仗。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to enter the city with Dun'gu and collect weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys with Dun'gu into the city to collect weapons and armor.

sentences.zh: 城中人殺使者，立敦固為都統，劫府庫，掠居民，乘城拒守。

translations.literal: Men in the city killed the envoys, established Dun'gu as commander-in-chief, plundered the treasury, looted residents, mounted the walls, and resisted in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The city folk killed the envoys, made Dun'gu commander-in-chief, looted the treasury and civilians, and manned the walls in defiance.

sentences.zh: 太宗賞破張覺功及有功將士各有差。

translations.literal: The Taizong rewarded the achievement in defeating Zhang Jue and distinguished meritorious officers and soldiers each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong rewarded those who had defeated Zhang Jue and gave differing rewards to meritorious officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 初，張覺奔宋，入于燕京，宗望責宋人納叛人，且征軍糧。

translations.literal: At first, when Zhang Jue fled to Song and entered Yanjing, Zong Wang reproached the Song for harboring a rebel and also requisitioned military grain.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Jue fled to Song and entered Yanjing, Zong Wang reproached the Song for sheltering a rebel and demanded military provisions.

sentences.zh: 久不聞問，宗望欲移書督之，請空名宣頭千道，增信牌，安撫新降之民。

translations.literal: For a long time there was no word; Zong Wang wished to send letters urging them, and requested a thousand blank commission slips, additional trust tablets, and authority to pacify the newly submitted people.
translations.idiomatic: After long silence from the Song, Zong Wang wanted to send letters pressing them for a response. He asked for a thousand blank commission slips, additional trust tablets, and authority to pacify the newly submitted population.

sentences.zh: 詔以「新附長吏職員仍舊。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Officials and staff of newly attached territories shall remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "Officials and staff in newly attached territories shall keep their posts.

sentences.zh: 已命諸路轉輸軍糧，勿督于宋。

translations.literal: Orders have already been given for the various routes to transport military grain—do not press the Song for it.
translations.idiomatic: Grain transport along every route has already been ordered—do not press the Song.

sentences.zh: 給銀牌十、空名宣頭五十道。

translations.literal: Grant ten silver tablets and fifty blank commission slips.
translations.idiomatic: Grant ten silver trust tablets and fifty blank commission slips.

sentences.zh: 及遷、潤、來、隰四州人徙於瀋州者，俟畢農各複其業。」

translations.literal: For people of the four prefectures Qian, Run, Lai, and Xi who were moved to Shen Prefecture, when farming is finished each shall return to his livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: People relocated from the four prefectures of Qian, Run, Lai, and Xi to Shen Prefecture may resume their occupations after the harvest."

sentences.zh: 乃詔鹹州輸粟宗望軍。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued ordering Xian Prefecture to supply grain to Zong Wang's army.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Xian Prefecture to supply grain to Zong Wang's army.

sentences.zh: 張敦固以兵八千分四隊出戰，大敗。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun'gu with eight thousand troops divided into four companies came out to fight and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun'gu sortied with eight thousand men in four columns and was badly defeated.

sentences.zh: 宗望再三開諭，敦固等曰：「屢嘗拒戰，不敢遽降。」
