translations.literal: Zong Wang repeatedly explained and urged them; Dun'gu and the others said: "Having repeatedly resisted in battle, we dare not surrender abruptly."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang urged them repeatedly. Dun'gu and the others said, "We have fought you repeatedly and dare not surrender so quickly."

sentences.zh: 宗望許其望闕遙拜。

translations.literal: Zong Wang permitted them to face the palace and bow from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang allowed them to face the palace and bow from a distance.

sentences.zh: 敦固乃開其一門。

translations.literal: Dun'gu then opened one gate.
translations.idiomatic: Dun'gu then opened one of the gates.

sentences.zh: 宗望使闍母奏其事，乃下詔赦南京官民，大小罪皆釋之，官職如舊。

translations.literal: Zong Wang had Chanmu memorialize the matter; an edict was then issued pardoning the officials and people of the Southern Capital—crimes great and small were all forgiven, and offices restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang had Chanmu report the matter to court, and an edict pardoned all the officials and people of the Southern Capital, absolving crimes great and small and restoring offices as before.

sentences.zh: 別敕有司輕徭賦、勸稼穡，疆場之事，一決于宗望。

translations.literal: A separate edict ordered the offices to lighten corvée and taxes, encourage farming, and that border affairs were all to be decided by Zong Wang alone.
translations.idiomatic: A separate edict ordered officials to lighten taxes and corvée, encourage agriculture, and gave Zong Wang sole authority over frontier affairs.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「議索張覺及逋亡戶口于宋。

translations.literal: It also said: "Consider demanding Zhang Jue and fugitive household registers from the Song.
translations.idiomatic: It also said, "Consider demanding Zhang Jue and fugitive population registers from the Song.

sentences.zh: 聞此歲不登，若如舊征斂，恐民匱乏，度其糧數賦之。

translations.literal: Hearing that this year the harvest failed, if levies are collected as before, the people will likely be exhausted—estimate the amount of grain and levy accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Since the harvest has failed this year, collecting levies as before would likely impoverish the people—assess what grain is available and levy accordingly.

sentences.zh: 射糧軍願為民者，使複田裏。

translations.literal: For grain-supply archers who wish to become civilians, let them return to fields and villages.
translations.idiomatic: Archers who supplied grain and wish to become civilians may return to farming.

sentences.zh: 小大之事關白軍帥，無得專達朝廷。」

translations.literal: Small and great affairs are to be reported to the army commander; none may communicate directly with the court."
translations.idiomatic: All matters, large and small, must go through the army commander—nothing may be sent directly to court."

sentences.zh: 詔宗望曰：「選勳賢及有民望者為南京留守，及諸闕員，仍具姓名官階以聞。」

translations.literal: An edict to Zong Wang said: "Select men of merit and ability and those with popular standing to serve as garrison commanders of the Southern Capital and to fill other vacant posts; still submit names and official ranks for report."
translations.idiomatic: The court instructed Zong Wang, "Select meritorious, capable men with local standing to serve as Southern Capital garrison commander and fill other vacancies, and submit their names and ranks for approval."

sentences.zh: 是時，遷、潤、來、隰四州之民保山砦者甚眾，宗望乙選良吏招撫。

translations.literal: At this time many people of the four prefectures Qian, Run, Lai, and Xi were holding mountain forts; Zong Wang then selected capable officials to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many people from the four prefectures of Qian, Run, Lai, and Xi were holding out in mountain forts; Zong Wang selected capable officials to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The sovereign approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 上召宗望赴闕，而闍母克南京，兵執偽都統張敦固殺之，南京平。

translations.literal: The sovereign summoned Zong Wang to court; meanwhile Chanmu took the Southern Capital, troops seized the false commander-in-chief Zhang Dun'gu and killed him, and the Southern Capital was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zong Wang to court. Meanwhile Chanmu captured the Southern Capital; troops seized the self-appointed commander Zhang Dun'gu and executed him, and the Southern Capital was pacified.

sentences.zh: 赴京師。

translations.literal: He went to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 於是，宗翰請無割山西地與宋，斡魯亦言之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zong Han requested that Shanxi territory not be ceded to Song, and Wolu spoke likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zong Han asked that no Shanxi territory be ceded to the Song, and Wolu said the same.

sentences.zh: 闍母論奏宋渝盟有驗，不可不備。

translations.literal: Chanmu memorialized arguing that the Song's breach of the alliance was proven and that they could not fail to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Chanmu memorialized that the Song had clearly broken the treaty and that the Jin must prepare accordingly.

sentences.zh: 及宗望還軍，上曰：「征歲幣于宋，以銀二十萬兩、絹三十萬匹分賜爾軍及六部東京諸軍。」

translations.literal: When Zong Wang returned to the army, the sovereign said: "Requisition annual tribute from the Song and distribute two hundred thousand taels of silver and three hundred thousand bolts of silk among your army and the armies of the Six Departments and Eastern Capital."
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Wang returned to his army, the emperor said, "Collect annual tribute from the Song and distribute two hundred thousand taels of silver and three hundred thousand bolts of silk among your army and the Eastern Capital forces of the Six Departments."

sentences.zh: 宗望至軍，宋兵三千自海道來，破九寨，殺馬城縣戍將節度使度盧斡，取其銀牌兵仗及馬而去。

translations.literal: When Zong Wang reached the army, three thousand Song troops came by sea route, broke eight forts, killed the garrison commander and military commissioner Dulüwo of Macheng County, took his silver tablet, weapons, and horses, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Wang reached his army, three thousand Song troops came by sea, overran eight forts, killed Macheng County garrison commander and military commissioner Dulüwo, seized his silver tablet, weapons, and horses, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宗望索戶口，宋人弗言，且聞童貫、郭藥師治軍燕山。

translations.literal: Zong Wang demanded household registers; the Song men would not say, and it was heard that Tong Guan and Guo Yaoshi were drilling troops at Yanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang demanded population registers, but the Song gave no answer. He also heard that Tong Guan and Guo Yaoshi were training troops at Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 宗望奏請伐宋曰：「苟不先之，恐為後患。」

translations.literal: Zong Wang memorialized requesting an attack on Song, saying: "If we do not strike first, I fear later trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang memorialized asking to attack the Song: "If we do not strike first, I fear later trouble."

sentences.zh: 宗翰亦以為方。

translations.literal: Zong Han also considered it the right plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han agreed that this was the right course.

sentences.zh: 故伐宋之策，宗望實啟之。

translations.literal: Thus the plan to attack Song was in fact initiated by Zong Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zong Wang was the one who truly launched the campaign against the Song.

sentences.zh: 宗望為南京路都統，闍母副之，自燕山路伐宋。

translations.literal: Zong Wang served as commander-in-chief of the Southern Capital Circuit, with Chanmu as deputy, attacking Song by the Yan Mountains route.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang was made commander-in-chief of the Southern Capital Circuit with Chanmu as his deputy, and marched against the Song by the Yan Mountains route.

sentences.zh: 宗望奏曰：「闍母于臣為叔父，請以闍母為都統，臣監戰事。」

translations.literal: Zong Wang memorialized: "Chanmu is my uncle—I ask that Chanmu be made commander-in-chief and that I supervise military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang memorialized, "Chanmu is my uncle; I ask that he be made commander-in-chief while I supervise the fighting."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The sovereign approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 以宗望監闍母、劉彥宗兩軍戰事。

translations.literal: Zong Wang was appointed to supervise the military affairs of Chanmu's and Liu Yanzong's two armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang was placed in charge of operations for the armies of Chanmu and Liu Yanzong.

sentences.zh: 宗望至三河，破郭藥師兵四萬五千于白河，蒲莧敗宋兵三千于古北口，郭藥師降。

translations.literal: Zong Wang reached Sanhe, defeated Guo Yaoshi's forty-five thousand troops at the White River, Puxian defeated three thousand Song troops at Gubeikou, and Guo Yaoshi surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Sanhe Zong Wang shattered Guo Yaoshi's forty-five-thousand-man army at the White River; Puxian routed three thousand Song troops at Gubeikou; and Guo Yaoshi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遂取燕山府，盡收其軍實，馬萬匹、甲胄五萬、兵七萬，州縣悉平。

translations.literal: He then took Yan Mountains Prefecture, gathered all its military stores—ten thousand horses, fifty thousand suits of armor, seventy thousand soldiers—and all prefectures and counties were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Yan Mountains Prefecture and seized all its military stores: ten thousand horses, fifty thousand suits of armor, and seventy thousand soldiers; every prefecture and county submitted.

sentences.zh: 宋中山戍將王彥、劉璧率兵二千來降。

translations.literal: The Song garrison commanders of Zhongshan Wang Yan and Liu Bi led two thousand troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Song garrison commanders Wang Yan and Liu Bi of Zhongshan led two thousand men to surrender.

sentences.zh: 蒲察、繩果以三百騎遇中山三萬人於厄隘之地，力戰，死之。

translations.literal: Pucha and Shengguo with three hundred cavalry met thirty thousand men from Zhongshan at a narrow pass, fought fiercely, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha and Shengguo with three hundred horsemen met thirty thousand men from Zhongshan at a narrow defile, fought to the last, and were killed.

sentences.zh: 術烈速、活裏改軍繼至，殺二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Shiliesu and Huoligai's army arrived afterward and killed more than twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliesu and Huoligai arrived with the main force and killed more than twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 宗望破宋真定兵五千人，遂克信德府，次邯鄲。

translations.literal: Zong Wang defeated five thousand Song troops of Zhending, then took Xinde Prefecture, and halted at Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang defeated five thousand Song troops from Zhending, captured Xinde Prefecture, and encamped at Handan.

sentences.zh: 宋李鄴請修舊好。

translations.literal: The Song Li Ye requested restoration of the old friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye of the Song asked to restore the former friendship.

sentences.zh: 宗望留軍中不遣。

translations.literal: Zong Wang detained him in the army and did not send him back.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang kept him in camp and would not release him.

sentences.zh: 自郭藥師降，益知宋之虛實。

translations.literal: From the time Guo Yaoshi surrendered, he came to know more fully the strengths and weaknesses of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guo Yaoshi surrendered, he learned far more about Song's actual strength and weakness.

sentences.zh: 宗望請以為燕京留守。

translations.literal: Zong Wang requested that he be made garrison commander of Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang asked that he be made garrison commander of Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 及董才降，益知宋之地裏。

translations.literal: When Dong Cai also surrendered, he came to know more fully the geography of Song territory.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Cai also surrendered, he gained a fuller knowledge of Song territory.

sentences.zh: 宗望請任以軍事。

translations.literal: Zong Wang requested that he be entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang asked that he be given military command.

sentences.zh: 太宗俱賜姓完顏氏，皆給以金牌。

translations.literal: The Taizong bestowed upon both the surname Wanyan and granted each a gold tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong granted both men the Wanyan surname and awarded each a gold tablet.

sentences.zh: 四年正月己巳，諸軍渡河，取滑州。

translations.literal: On the jisi day of the first month of the fourth year, the armies crossed the river and took Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the first month of the fourth year, the armies crossed the Yellow River and captured Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 使吳孝民入汴，以詔書問納平州張覺事，令執送童貫、譚積、詹度，以黃河為界，納質奉貢。

translations.literal: He sent Wu Xiaomin into Bian to question with an edict the matter of the Song harboring Zhang Jue of Ping Prefecture, ordering them to arrest and send Tong Guan, Tan Ji, and Zhan Du, take the Yellow River as the boundary, and send hostages and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wu Xiaomin into Bian with an edict demanding an accounting for sheltering Zhang Jue of Ping Prefecture, requiring the handover of Tong Guan, Tan Ji, and Zhan Du, establishing the Yellow River as the border, and demanding hostages and tribute.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，諸軍圍汴。

translations.literal: On guiyou the armies besieged Bian.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the armies besieged Bian.

sentences.zh: 宋少帝請為伯侄國，效質納地，增歲幣請和。

translations.literal: The Song Shaodi requested to become a nephew state, send hostages and cede territory, increase annual tribute, and sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor asked to become a nephew state to the Jin, send hostages, cede territory, increase annual tribute, and sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 遂割太原、中山、河間三鎮，書用伯侄禮，以康王構、太宰張邦昌為質。

translations.literal: He then ceded the three garrisons of Taiyuan, Zhongshan, and Hejian, used nephew-state protocol in documents, and sent Prince Kang Gou and Grand Chancellor Zhang Bangchang as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: The Song ceded the three garrisons of Taiyuan, Zhongshan, and Hejian, agreed to nephew-state protocol in official correspondence, and sent Prince Kang Gou and Grand Chancellor Zhang Bangchang as hostages.

sentences.zh: 沈晦以哲書、三鎮地圖至軍中，發幣割地一依定約，語在宋事中。

translations.literal: Shen Hui brought the imperial letter and maps of the three garrisons to the army; tribute was disbursed and territory ceded all according to the fixed agreement—the account is in the Song annals.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Hui brought the imperial letter and maps of the three garrisons to the Jin camp; tribute was paid and territory ceded as agreed—the full account appears in the Song annals.

sentences.zh: 二月丁酉朔，與宋平，退軍孟陽。

translations.literal: On the first dingyou day of the second month peace was made with Song, and the army withdrew to Mengyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the second month, dingyou, peace was made with the Song and the army withdrew to Mengyang.

sentences.zh: 是夜，姚平仲兵四十萬來襲。

translations.literal: That night Yao Pingzhong with four hundred thousand troops came to attack by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yao Pingzhong launched a surprise attack with four hundred thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 候騎覺之，分遣諸將迎擊，大破平仲軍，複進攻汴城，問舉兵之狀。

translations.literal: Scout horsemen detected them; generals were dispatched separately to meet the attack, Yao Pingzhong's army was greatly defeated, they again advanced to attack Bian city, and asked the circumstances of raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Scout riders detected the movement; commanders were sent out to intercept and smashed Yao Pingzhong's army. The Jin forces again advanced on Bian and demanded an explanation for the attack.

sentences.zh: 少帝大恐，使宇文虛中來辨曰：「初不知其事，且將加罪其人。」

translations.literal: The Shaodi was greatly terrified and sent Yuwen Xuzhong to explain: "At first we did not know of this matter, and we shall moreover punish those responsible."
translations.idiomatic: The Song emperor was terrified and sent Yuwen Xuzhong to explain, "We knew nothing of this in advance, and we will punish those responsible."

sentences.zh: 宗望輟弗攻，改肅王樞為質，康王構遣歸。

translations.literal: Zong Wang paused and did not attack; Prince Su Shu was substituted as hostage and Prince Kang Gou was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang held off the assault, replaced Prince Su Shu as hostage, and sent Prince Kang Gou home.

sentences.zh: 師還，河北兩鎮不下，遂分兵討之。

translations.literal: The army returned; two garrisons in Hebei did not submit, so troops were divided to subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: As the army withdrew, two Hebei garrisons still held out, so forces were divided to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 宗望罷常勝軍，給還燕人田業，命將士分屯安肅、雄、霸、廣信之境。

translations.literal: Zong Wang disbanded the Ever-Victorious Army, returned Yan people's fields and estates, and ordered officers and soldiers to garrison separately in the territories of Ansu, Xiong, Ba, and Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang disbanded the Ever-Victorious Army, restored land to the people of Yan, and ordered troops to garrison the regions of Ansu, Xiong, Ba, and Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 宗望還山西。

translations.literal: Zong Wang returned to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang returned to Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 未幾。

translations.literal: Before long.
translations.idiomatic: Before long.

sentences.zh: 為右副元帥，有功將士遷賞有差。

translations.literal: He was made Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief; officers and soldiers with merit were promoted and rewarded according to their achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Deputy Commander-in-Chief, and meritorious officers and soldiers were promoted and rewarded in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 頃之，宋少帝以書誘餘睹，肅仲恭獻其書，詔複伐宋。

translations.literal: Before long, the Song Lesser Emperor used a letter to entice Yudu; Su Zhonggong presented the letter, and an edict ordered another campaign against Song.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Song Lesser Emperor tried to win Yudu over by letter; Su Zhonggong presented the letter, and an edict ordered a renewed attack on Song.

sentences.zh: 八月，宗望會諸將，發自保州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Zong Wang assembled the generals and set out from Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zong Wang gathered his generals and marched out from Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 耶律鐸破敵兵三萬於雄州，殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: Yelü Duo defeated thirty thousand enemy troops at Xiong Prefecture and killed more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiong Prefecture Yelü Duo routed thirty thousand enemy troops and killed more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 那野敗宋軍七千於中山。

translations.literal: Naye defeated seven thousand Song troops at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Naye defeated seven thousand Song troops at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 高六、董才破宋兵三千於廣信。

translations.literal: Gao Liu and Dong Cai defeated three thousand Song troops at Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Liu and Dong Cai defeated three thousand Song soldiers at Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 宋種師閔軍四萬人駐井陘，宗望大破之，遂取天威軍。

translations.literal: The Song commander Zhong Shimin with forty thousand troops was stationed at Jingxing; Zong Wang greatly defeated him and then took Tianwei Army.
translations.idiomatic: Song general Zhong Shimin had forty thousand men at Jingxing; Zong Wang routed him and then captured Tianwei Army.

sentences.zh: 東還，遂克真定，殺知府李邈，得戶三萬，降五縣。

translations.literal: Returning east, he then took Zhending, killed prefect Li Miao, obtained thirty thousand households, and reduced five counties.
translations.idiomatic: Marching east, he took Zhending, executed Prefect Li Miao, gained thirty thousand households, and received the submission of five counties.

sentences.zh: 遂自真定趨汴。

translations.literal: He then pressed from Zhending toward Bian.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhending he then pressed on toward Bian.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊辰，宗望至河上，降魏縣。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the eleventh month Zong Wang reached the river and reduced Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the eleventh month Zong Wang reached the Yellow River and reduced Wei County.

sentences.zh: 諸軍渡河，留諸將分出大名之境。

translations.literal: The armies crossed the river; generals were left behind to spread out through the territory of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: The armies crossed the river, and Zong Wang left his generals to spread out across the Daming region.

sentences.zh: 降臨河縣，至大名縣，德清軍、開德府，皆克之。

translations.literal: He reduced Linhe County, reached Daming County, and captured Deqing Army and Kaide Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced Linhe County, reached Daming County, and captured Deqing Army and Kaide Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 阿裏刮以騎兵三千先趨汴，破宋軍六千于路。

translations.literal: Aligua with three thousand cavalry pressed first toward Bian and defeated six thousand Song troops on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Aligua led three thousand horsemen ahead toward Bian and defeated six thousand Song troops along the way.

sentences.zh: 取胙城，抵汴城下，覆宋兵千人，擒數將。

translations.literal: He took Zuo City, reached below Bian city, routed one thousand Song troops, and captured several generals.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zuo City, reached the walls of Bian, routed a thousand Song soldiers, and captured several commanders.

sentences.zh: 宗望至汴，分遣諸將遏宋援兵，奔睹、那野、賽刺、台實連破宋援兵。

translations.literal: When Zong Wang reached Bian, he dispatched generals separately to block Song relief troops; Bendu, Naye, Saici, and Taishi in succession defeated Song relief forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Wang reached Bian he sent his generals to block Song relief columns; Bendu, Naye, Saici, and Taishi defeated them one after another.

sentences.zh: 閏月壬辰朔，宋兵一萬出自汴城來戰。

translations.literal: On the first renchen day of the intercalary month, ten thousand Song troops came out from Bian city to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the intercalary month, renchen, ten thousand Song troops marched out of Bian to fight.

sentences.zh: 宗望選勁勇五千，使當海、忽魯、雛鶻失擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zong Wang selected five thousand picked warriors and had Danghai, Hulu, and Chugushi strike and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang picked five thousand elite troops and sent Danghai, Hulu, and Chugushi to rout them.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，宗翰自太原會軍於汴。

translations.literal: On the guisi day Zong Han from Taiyuan joined the army at Bian.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Zong Han marched from Taiyuan and joined the army at Bian.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，克汴州。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day he took Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen he captured Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，宋少帝詣軍前。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day the Song Lesser Emperor came to the front of the army.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the Song Lesser Emperor came before the Jin army.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸亥，宋帝奉表降。

translations.literal: On the guihai day of the twelfth month the Song emperor submitted a memorial of surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai in the twelfth month the Song emperor submitted his surrender memorial.

sentences.zh: 上使勖就軍中勞賜宗翰、宗望，使皆執其手以勞之。

translations.literal: The sovereign sent Xu to the army to console and reward Zong Han and Zong Wang, and had him take each by the hand in consolation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xu to the army to console and reward Zong Han and Zong Wang, bidding him take each by the hand in person.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，以宋二主及其宗族四百七十餘人，及珪璋、寶印、袞冕、車輅、祭器、大樂、靈台、圖書，與大軍北還。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, with the two Song rulers and more than four hundred seventy of their clansmen, together with jade scepters and seals, robes and caps, carriages, ritual vessels, great music, observatories, and books, they returned north with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 5 they marched north with the main army, taking the two Song emperors and more than four hundred seventy members of their clan, along with jade regalia, imperial seals, robes and caps, carriages, ritual vessels, the great music, observatory instruments, and the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 宗望乃分諸將鎮守河北。

translations.literal: Zong Wang then assigned generals separately to garrison Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang then posted his generals to garrison Hebei.

sentences.zh: 董才降廣信軍及旁近縣鎮。

translations.literal: Dong Cai reduced Guangxin Army and the nearby counties and garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Cai received the submission of Guangxin Army and the neighboring counties and garrisons.

sentences.zh: 宗望乃西上涼陘。

translations.literal: Zong Wang then went west up Liang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang then marched west through Liang Pass.

sentences.zh: 詔宗望曰：「自河之北，今既分畫，重念其民見城邑有被殘者，遂阻命堅守，其申諭招輯安全之。

translations.literal: An edict to Zong Wang said: "North of the river, now that boundaries have been drawn, I deeply consider that among the people some saw their towns ravaged and therefore resisted orders and held firm; proclaim and explain to them, win them over, and keep them safe.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Zong Wang read: "North of the river, now that the borders have been fixed, I am mindful that some people saw their towns ravaged and therefore resisted and held out; explain the situation to them, win them over, and keep them secure.

sentences.zh: 儻堅執不移，自當致討。

translations.literal: If they stubbornly refuse to move, then of course we shall punish them.
translations.idiomatic: If they stubbornly refuse to yield, then of course we shall move against them.

sentences.zh: 若諸軍敢利於俘掠，輒肆毀蕩者，當底於罰。」

translations.literal: If any army dares to profit from plunder and wantonly destroy and lay waste, it shall be punished to the full."
translations.idiomatic: If any army dares to profit from looting and wantonly destroy and ravage the land, it shall be punished without mercy."

sentences.zh: 初。

translations.literal: At first.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier.

sentences.zh: 遼帝之奔陰山也，遼節度使和尚與林牙馬哥、男慎思俱被擒，都統杲使阿鄰護送得裏底、和尚、雅裏斯等入京師。

translations.literal: When the Liao emperor fled to Yinshan, the Liao military commissioner Heshang together with Linya Mage and Nan Shensi were all captured; Commander-in-Chief Gao had A Lin escort Delidi, Heshang, Yalisi, and others into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao emperor fled to Yinshan, Liao military commissioner Heshang was captured along with Linya Mage and Nan Shensi; Commander-in-Chief Gao had A Lin escort Delidi, Heshang, Yalisi, and the others to the capital.

sentences.zh: 得裏底道亡，太祖誅阿鄰。

translations.literal: Delidi fled on the road; the Taizu executed A Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Delidi escaped en route, and the Taizu had A Lin executed.

sentences.zh: 和尚弟道溫為興中尹，太祖使謾都本以兵千人與和尚往招之。

translations.literal: Heshang's younger brother Daowen was prefect of Xingzhong; the Taizu sent Manduben with one thousand troops together with Heshang to go and summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Heshang's younger brother Daowen was prefect of Xingzhong; the Taizu sent Manduben with a thousand troops to accompany Heshang and summon him.

sentences.zh: 和尚欲亡去，不克，至興中城下，以矢系書射城中，教道溫毋降。

translations.literal: Heshang wished to flee but could not; when he reached below Xingzhong city, he tied a letter to an arrow and shot it into the city, instructing Daowen not to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Heshang tried to escape but failed; when he reached the walls of Xingzhong he tied a letter to an arrow and shot it into the city, telling Daowen not to submit.

sentences.zh: 事泄，謾都本責之曰：「汝何反覆如此？」

translations.literal: The matter leaked out; Manduben rebuked him, saying: "Why are you so changeable?"
translations.idiomatic: The plot was discovered; Manduben rebuked him: "Why are you so fickle?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「以忠報國，何反覆之有，雖死不恨。」

translations.literal: He replied: "To repay the state with loyalty—what changeableness is there? Even in death I have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I am repaying the state with loyalty—where is the fickleness in that? Even if I die, I have no regret."

sentences.zh: 乃殺之。

translations.literal: They then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They then executed him.

sentences.zh: 既而宗望軍遇遼都統孛迭等，道溫在其中，相與隔水而語。

translations.literal: Before long Zong Wang's army encountered Liao commander-in-chief Bedie and others; Daowen was among them, and they spoke to one another across the water.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Zong Wang's army encountered Liao commander-in-chief Bedie and his men; Daowen was among them, and they spoke to one another from opposite banks.

sentences.zh: 宗望承制招之，孛迭唯諾，無降意。

translations.literal: Zong Wang, acting on imperial authority, summoned them; Bedie assented, but had no intention of surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang, acting on imperial authority, summoned them to submit; Bedie agreed in words but showed no sign of surrendering.

sentences.zh: 宗望謂道溫曰：「汝兄和尚因戰而獲，未嘗加罪，後以叛誅，能無痛悼。」

translations.literal: Zong Wang said to Daowen: "Your elder brother Heshang was taken in battle and was never punished; later he was executed for rebellion—can you feel no grief?"
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang said to Daowen: "Your brother Heshang was captured in battle and was never punished; later he was executed for rebellion—surely you must grieve."

sentences.zh: 道溫曰：「吾兄辱于見獲，榮于死國。」

translations.literal: Daowen said: "My elder brother was shamed in being captured and honored in dying for the state."
translations.idiomatic: Daowen replied: "My brother was shamed by capture and honored by dying for his country."

sentences.zh: 宗望顧馬和尚曰：「能為我取此乎？」

translations.literal: Zong Wang turned to Ma Heshang and said: "Can you take this man for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wang turned to Ma Heshang and asked: "Can you take him for me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「能。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I can."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I can."

sentences.zh: 遂以所部渡水擊敗其眾，直趨道溫，射中其臂，獲而殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon with his own unit he crossed the water, defeated their force, went straight at Daowen, shot him in the arm, captured him, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he crossed the water with his own troops, routed the enemy, charged straight at Daowen, shot him in the arm, captured him, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 子 齊 京 文

translations.literal: Sons: Qi, Jing, Wen
translations.idiomatic: Sons: Qi, Jing, and Wen

sentences.zh: 弟京、弟文皆以謀反誅。

translations.literal: The younger brothers Jing and Wen were both executed for plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The younger brothers Jing and Wen were both put to death for plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 世宗盡以其家財產與齊之子咬住。

translations.literal: The Shizong gave all their family property to Qi's son Yaozhu.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizong gave all of their family property to Qi's son Yaozhu.

sentences.zh: 詔齊妻曰：「汝等皆當緣坐，有至大辟及流竄者。

translations.literal: An edict to Qi's wife said: "You all should suffer guilt by association; some deserve capital punishment or exile.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to Qi's wife read: "You should all suffer guilt by association; some of you merit execution or banishment.

sentences.zh: 朕念宋王，故置而不問，且以其家產賜汝子。

translations.literal: I think of Prince Song and therefore leave the matter unpunished, and moreover give their family property to your son.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for Prince Song I am leaving the matter unpunished, and I am moreover granting their family property to your son.

sentences.zh: 宜悉朕意。」

translations.literal: You should fully understand my intent."
translations.idiomatic: You should understand my intent fully."

sentences.zh: 十五年，上召英王爽謂曰：「卿于讀者公主女子中為咬住擇婚，其禮幣命有司給之。」

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the sovereign summoned Prince Ying Shuang and said: "Among the princesses' daughters at the Reader's Office, choose a marriage for Yaozhu; let the relevant offices supply the betrothal gifts."
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 the emperor summoned Prince Ying Shuang and said: "Among the princesses' daughters at the Reader's Office, choose a wife for Yaozhu; the relevant offices shall supply the betrothal gifts."

sentences.zh: 俄襲叔父京山東西路徒毋堅猛安。

translations.literal: Before long he inherited his uncle Jing's Shandong East-West Route Tumu Jian Meng'an post.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he inherited his uncle Jing's post as Tumu Jian Meng'an on the Shandong East-West Route.

sentences.zh: 京本名忽魯，以宗室子累遷特進。

translations.literal: Jing's original name was Hulu; as a member of the imperial clan he was repeatedly promoted to Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's original name was Hulu; as an imperial clansman he rose by stages to Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，除翰林學士承旨，兼修國史，加開府儀同三司，遷工部尚書，改禮部、兵禮部，判大宗正事，封曹王，除河間尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he was made Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy, concurrently compiling the national history; he was given the rank of Grand Preceptor with the privilege of an opening office equal to the Three Excellencies, transferred to Minister of Works, changed to Minister of Rites and Minister of Military Rites, adjudicated affairs of the Great Clan Court, was enfeoffed as Prince of Cao, and appointed prefect of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 2 he was made Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy and concurrently charged with compiling the national history; he received the rank of Grand Preceptor with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, was transferred to Minister of Works, then Minister of Rites and Minister of Military Rites, adjudicated affairs of the Great Clan Court, was enfeoffed as Prince of Cao, and appointed prefect of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，例封瀋國公，北京留守，以喪去官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong, by precedent he was enfeoffed as Duke of Shen and made Northern Capital garrison commander; he left office on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 2, by precedent he was enfeoffed Duke of Shen and made Northern Capital garrison commander; he left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 起複益都尹。

translations.literal: He was recalled from mourning to serve as prefect of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled from mourning and appointed prefect of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 六年，坐違制，立春日與徒單貞飲酒，降灤州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, for violating regulations by drinking wine with Tushan Zhen on the day of the Beginning of Spring, he was demoted to prefect of Luan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, for violating regulations by drinking with Tushan Zhen on the Beginning of Spring, he was demoted to prefect of Luan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改絳陽軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to military commissioner of Jiangyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to military commissioner of Jiangyang Army.

sentences.zh: 海陵遣護衛忽魯往絳州殺之。

translations.literal: Hailing sent the guard Hulu to Jiang Prefecture to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing sent the guard Hulu to Jiang Prefecture to kill him.

sentences.zh: 京由間道走入汾州境得免。

translations.literal: Jing escaped by a hidden route into the territory of Fen Prefecture and got away.
translations.idiomatic: Jing fled by a back road into Fen Prefecture and escaped.

sentences.zh: 京到西京，京妻嘗召日者孫邦榮推京祿命。

translations.literal: When Jing reached Western Capital, Jing's wife had summoned the day-reader Sun Bangrong to cast Jing's fortune in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing reached Western Capital, his wife had summoned the fortune-teller Sun Bangrong to read Jing's official destiny.

sentences.zh: 邦榮言留守官至太師，爵封王。

translations.literal: Bangrong said that as garrison commander his rank would reach Grand Preceptor and his title would be enfeoffed as king.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrong said that as garrison commander he would rise to Grand Preceptor and be enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 京問：「此上更無否？」

translations.literal: Jing asked: "Is there nothing beyond this?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing asked: "Is there nothing higher than this?"

sentences.zh: 邦榮曰：「止於此。」

translations.literal: Bangrong said: "It stops here."
translations.idiomatic: Bangrong said: "It stops there."

sentences.zh: 京曰：「若止於此，所官何為。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "If it stops here, what is the point of holding office?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing said: "If that is all, what is the point of holding office?"

sentences.zh: 邦榮察其意，乃詐為圖讖，作詩，中有「鶻魯為」之語，以獻於京。

translations.literal: Bangrong perceived his intent and therefore falsely made prognostic charts, composed a poem containing the phrase "Hulu wei," and presented it to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrong saw what he wanted and forged a prophecy, composing a poem with the phrase "Hulu wei" and presenting it to Jing.

sentences.zh: 京曰：「後誠如此乎。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Will it truly be like this afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing said: "Will it truly come to pass?"

sentences.zh: 遂受其詩，再使卜之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he accepted the poem and had him cast the lots again.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted the poem and had him cast the lots again.

sentences.zh: 邦榮稱所得卦有獨權之兆。

translations.literal: Bangrong said the hexagram obtained showed an omen of sole authority.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrong declared that the hexagram showed an omen of sole authority.

sentences.zh: 京複使邦榮推世宗當生年月。

translations.literal: Jing again had Bangrong calculate the month and year of the Shizong's destined lifespan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing again had Bangrong calculate the month and year of the Shizong's destined end.

sentences.zh: 家人孫小哥妄作謠言誑惑京，如邦榮指，京信之。

translations.literal: A household servant, Sun Xiaoge, fabricated rumors to deceive Jing; just as Bangrong indicated, Jing believed it.
translations.idiomatic: A household servant, Sun Xiaoge, spread false rumors to deceive Jing; just as Bangrong had indicated, Jing believed them.

sentences.zh: 京妻公壽具知其事。

translations.literal: Jing's wife Gongshou knew the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's wife Gongshou knew the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 大定五年三月，孫邦榮上變。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year of Dading, Sun Bangrong reported the plot.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Dading 5, Sun Bangrong reported the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 詔刑部侍郎高德基、戶部員外郎完顏兀古出往鞫之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Minister of Justice Gao Deji and Outer Office Member of the Ministry of Revenue Wanyan Wuguchu to go and interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Vice Minister of Justice Gao Deji and Outer Office Member of the Ministry of Revenue Wanyan Wuguchu to go and investigate.

sentences.zh: 京等皆款伏。

translations.literal: Jing and the others all confessed fully.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and the others all confessed in full.

sentences.zh: 獄成，還奏。

translations.literal: When the case was complete they returned and reported.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was closed they returned and reported.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「海陵無道，使光英在，朕亦保全之，況京等哉。」

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "Hailing was without the Way; if Guangying were alive, I would also have preserved him—how much more Jing and the others!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Hailing lost the Way; if Guangying were alive, I would have spared him too—how much more Jing and the others!"

sentences.zh: 於是，京夫婦特免死，杖一百，除名，嵐州樓煩縣安置，以奴婢百口自隨，官給上田。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jing and his wife were specially spared death, beaten one hundred strokes, struck from the rolls, and settled at Loufan County in Lan Prefecture, allowed one hundred male and female servants to accompany them, with official grants of superior fields.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jing and his wife were specially spared execution, beaten one hundred strokes, struck from the rolls, and exiled to Loufan County in Lan Prefecture with a hundred servants; the state granted them superior fields.

sentences.zh: 遣兀古出、劉珫宣諭京，詔曰：「朕與汝皆太祖之孫。

translations.literal: Wuguchu and Liu Kun were sent to announce the edict to Jing; the edict said: "You and I are both grandsons of the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Wuguchu and Liu Kun were sent to announce the edict to Jing, which read: "You and I are both grandsons of the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 海陵失道，翦滅宗支，朕念兄弟無幾，于汝尤為親愛，汝亦自知之，何為而懷此心。

translations.literal: Hailing lost the Way and cut down the imperial line; I think how few brothers remain, and toward you I am especially affectionate—you know this yourself—so why harbor such a heart?
translations.idiomatic: Hailing lost the Way and slaughtered the imperial line; I know how few brothers remain, and I am especially fond of you—you know this yourself—so why did you harbor such thoughts?

sentences.zh: 朕念骨肉，不忍盡法。

translations.literal: I think of our kinship and cannot bear to apply the full penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for our kinship I cannot bring myself to apply the full penalty.

sentences.zh: 汝若尚不思過，朕雖不加誅，天地豈能容汝也。」

translations.literal: If you still do not reflect on your faults, even if I do not execute you, how could Heaven and Earth contain you?"
translations.idiomatic: If you still refuse to repent, even if I do not put you to death, Heaven and Earth will not tolerate you."

sentences.zh: 十年四月，詔于樓煩縣，為京作第一區，月給節度廩俸。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year, an edict ordered that at Loufan County a first-class residence district be made for Jing, with a monthly stipend at the level of a military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 10, an edict ordered a first-class residence built for Jing at Loufan County and granted him a monthly stipend at the level of a military governor.

sentences.zh: 十二年，兄德州防禦使文謀反。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year his elder brother Wen, Defender of Dezhou, plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 his elder brother Wen, Defender of Dezhou, plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上問皇太子、趙王允中及宰臣曰：「京謀不軌，朕特免死，今複當緣坐，何如。」

translations.literal: The sovereign asked the crown prince, Prince Zhao Yunzhong, and the chief ministers: "Jing plotted treason; I specially spared his life—now should he again suffer guilt by association? What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the crown prince, Prince Zhao Yunzhong, and the chief ministers: "Jing plotted treason and I specially spared his life—should he now again suffer guilt by association? What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 宰臣或言京圖逆，今不除之，恐為後患。

translations.literal: Some chief ministers said Jing intended rebellion; if he were not removed now, they feared he would be a future trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers said Jing had plotted rebellion; if he were not removed now, they feared future trouble.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「天下大器歸於有德，海陵失道，朕乃得之。

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "The great vessel of the realm goes to the virtuous; Hailing lost the Way, and I obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The throne belongs to the virtuous; Hailing lost the Way, and I won it.

sentences.zh: 但務修德，余何足慮。」

translations.literal: If we only cultivate virtue, what else is there to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: If we devote ourselves to virtue, what else is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「誠如聖訓。」

translations.literal: The crown prince said: "It is truly as Your Majesty teaches."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said: "It is exactly as Your Majesty teaches."

sentences.zh: 乃遣使宣諭京，詔曰：「卿兄文，舊封國公，不任職事，朕進封王爵，委以大籓。

translations.literal: Thereupon an envoy was sent to announce to Jing; the edict said: "Your elder brother Wen was formerly enfeoffed as a state duke and held no office; I advanced him to princely rank and entrusted him with a great fief.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was then sent to announce to Jing; the edict read: "Your elder brother Wen was formerly enfeoffed a state duke and held no office; I raised him to princely rank and entrusted him with a great fief.

sentences.zh: 頃在大名，以贓得罪，止削左遷，不知恩幸，乃蓄怨心，謀不軌，罪及兄弟。

translations.literal: Recently at Daming he was guilty of corruption; I only stripped his rank and demoted him—he did not know this favor—and so he harbored resentment and plotted treason, bringing guilt upon his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Recently at Daming he was convicted of corruption; I only stripped his rank and demoted him—he did not recognize this mercy—and so he nursed resentment, plotted treason, and brought guilt upon his brothers.

sentences.zh: 朕念宋王，皆免緣坐。

translations.literal: I think of Prince Song and exempt you all from guilt by association.
translations.idiomatic: Out of regard for Prince Song I exempt you all from guilt by association.

sentences.zh: 文之家產應沒入者，盡與卿兄子咬住。

translations.literal: Wen's family property that should have been confiscated is all given to your elder brother's son Yaozhu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's confiscated property is all given to your elder brother's son Yaozhu.

sentences.zh: 卿宜悉此意。」

translations.literal: You should fully understand this intent."
translations.idiomatic: You should understand this fully."

sentences.zh: 二十年十一月，上問宰臣曰：「京之罪始于其妻，妄卜休咎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twentieth year the sovereign asked the chief ministers: "Jing's offense began with his wife's reckless divination of fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 20 the emperor asked the chief ministers: "Jing's crime began with his wife's reckless fortune-telling.

sentences.zh: 太祖諸孫存者無幾，朕欲召置左右，不使任職，但廩給之，卿等以為何如？」

translations.literal: Few of the Taizu's grandsons still survive; I wish to summon him and keep him at my side, not appoint him to office but only supply his rations—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Few of the Taizu's grandsons still survive; I wish to summon Jing and keep him near me, give him no office but only maintain him—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「置之近密，臣等以為非宜。」

translations.literal: They all said: "To place him close and intimate—we think it inappropriate."
translations.idiomatic: They all said: "To keep him close at hand—we think it unwise."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕若修德，何以豫懷疑忌。」

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "If I cultivate virtue, why should I pre-emptively harbor suspicion and jealousy?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If I cultivate virtue, why should I live in suspicion and jealousy beforehand?"

sentences.zh: 久之，上複欲召京，宰臣曰：「京，不赦之罪也，赦之以為至幸矣，豈可複。」

translations.literal: After a long while the sovereign again wished to summon Jing; the chief ministers said: "Jing committed an unpardonable crime; to pardon him was already the utmost favor—how could he be summoned again?"
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence the emperor again wished to summon Jing; the chief ministers said: "Jing committed an unpardonable crime; to spare him was already the greatest mercy—how could he be recalled again?"

sentences.zh: 上默良久，乃止。

translations.literal: The sovereign was silent a long while and then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell silent for a long while and then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 文本名胡刺。

translations.literal: Wen's original name was Huaci.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's original name was Huaci.

sentences.zh: 皇統間，授世襲謀克，加奉國上將軍，居中京。

translations.literal: During the Huangtong era he was granted a hereditary Meng'an post, promoted to Defender-in-Chief of the State, and stationed at the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangtong era he received a hereditary Meng'an commission, was made Defender-in-Chief of the State, and resided at the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，賜錢二萬貫。

translations.literal: When Hailing usurped the throne, he granted Wen twenty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing seized the throne, he rewarded Wen with twenty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 是時，左淵為中京轉運使，市中有穢術敲仙者，文與淵皆與之遊。

translations.literal: At that time Zuo Yuan was transport commissioner of the Central Capital; in the market there was a filthy practitioner called Qiaoxian, and both Wen and Yuan associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zuo Yuan was transport commissioner of the Central Capital. A disreputable street diviner called Qiaoxian was active in the markets, and both Wen and Yuan kept company with him.

sentences.zh: 海陵還中京，聞，召敲仙詰問，窮竟本末。

translations.literal: When Hailing returned to the Central Capital and heard of it, he summoned Qiaoxian for interrogation and investigated the matter to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing returned to the Central Capital and heard of it, he summoned Qiaoxian for questioning and traced the affair to its roots.

sentences.zh: 既而殺之於市，責讓文、淵。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he executed Qiaoxian in the market and rebuked Wen and Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Qiaoxian executed in the market and rebuked Wen and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，除秘書，坐與靈壽縣主阿裏虎有奸，杖二百，除名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he was appointed to the Secretariat; for adultery with the Princess of Lingshou, Aligu, he received two hundred strokes of the staff and was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1 he was appointed to the Secretariat, but for an affair with Princess Aligu of Lingshou he was given two hundred strokes of the staff and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 俄複為秘書監，封王。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed as a prince.

sentences.zh: 正隆例封鄖國公，以喪去官。

translations.literal: Under the Zhenglong precedent he was enfeoffed Duke of Yun and left office to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhenglong precedent he was made Duke of Yun and left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 起複翰林學士承旨、同判大宗正事、昌武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning, he became Hanlin academician-expositor, associate director of the Great Clan Directorate, and military commissioner of Changwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he became Hanlin academician-expositor, associate director of the Great Clan Directorate, and military commissioner of Changwu Army.

sentences.zh: 文到大名，多取猛安謀克良馬，或以駑馬易之，買民物與價不盡其直。

translations.literal: When Wen reached Daming, he took many fine horses from the Meng'an and Mouke, sometimes exchanging them for poor horses, and when buying goods from the people he did not pay the full price.
translations.idiomatic: At Daming Wen seized many fine horses from the Meng'an and Mouke, sometimes swapping them for nags, and when buying from commoners he paid less than the fair price.

sentences.zh: 尋常占役弓手四十餘人，詭納稅草十六萬束。

translations.literal: He routinely impressed more than forty bowmen for service and fraudulently reported payment of one hundred sixty thousand bundles of tax fodder.
translations.idiomatic: He routinely impressed more than forty bowmen for personal service and falsely reported delivery of one hundred sixty thousand bundles of tax fodder.

sentences.zh: 公用闕，取民錢一萬九千餘貫。

translations.literal: When public funds were short, he took more than nineteen thousand strings of cash from the people.
translations.idiomatic: When official funds ran short, he extorted more than nineteen thousand strings of cash from the populace.

sentences.zh: 坐是奪爵，降德州防禦使，僚佐皆坐不矯正解職。

translations.literal: For this his noble rank was stripped and he was demoted to defender of De Prefecture; his subordinates were all dismissed for failing to correct him.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was stripped of his noble rank and demoted to defender of De Prefecture; his subordinates were all dismissed for failing to rein him in.

sentences.zh: 監察禦史董師中按文事失糾察，已除尚書省都事，降沁南軍節度副使。

translations.literal: Censor Dong Shizhong, in investigating Wen's case, had failed to detect the offenses; though already appointed director in the Ministry of Revenue, he was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Qinnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Dong Shizhong had failed to uncover Wen's offenses during the investigation; though already appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue, he was demoted to deputy military commissioner of Qinnan Army.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自今長官不法，僚佐不矯正，又不言上，並嚴行懲斷。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "From now on, if a chief official breaks the law and his subordinates do not correct him and do not report upward, all shall be sternly punished."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Henceforth, if a chief official breaks the law and his subordinates neither correct him nor report it upward, all shall be punished severely."

sentences.zh: 文既失職，居常怏怏，日與家奴石抹合住、忽裏者為怨言。

translations.literal: After Wen lost his post he was constantly discontented, daily voicing complaints with his household slaves Shimoh Hezhu and Hulizhe.
translations.idiomatic: After Wen lost his post he brooded in discontent, daily airing grievances with his household slaves Shimoh Hezhu and Hulizhe.

sentences.zh: 合住揣知其意，因言南京路猛安阿古、合住、謀克頗裏，銀術可與大王厚善，果欲舉大事，彼皆願從。

translations.literal: Hezhu guessed his intent and therefore said: "On the Nanjing route the Meng'an Agu, Hezhu, and Mouke Poli, and Yinchuoke are on close terms with Your Highness; if you truly wish to undertake a great enterprise, they will all follow."
translations.idiomatic: Hezhu guessed his intent and said: "On the Nanjing route the Meng'an Agu, Hezhu, and Mouke Poli, and Yinchuoke are devoted to Your Highness. If you truly mean to raise a great enterprise, they will all follow you."

sentences.zh: 文信其言。

translations.literal: Wen believed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Wen believed him.

sentences.zh: 乃召日者康洪占休咎，密以謀告洪。

translations.literal: He then summoned the day-selector Kang Hong to divine fortune and misfortune and secretly told Hong the plot.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the diviner Kang Hong to read fortune and misfortune and secretly confided the plot to him.

sentences.zh: 洪言來歲甚吉。

translations.literal: Hong said the coming year was very auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Hong declared the coming year most auspicious.

sentences.zh: 文厚謝洪，使家僮剛哥等往南京以書幣遺阿古等。

translations.literal: Wen richly thanked Hong and sent his household servant Gangge and others to Nanjing with letters and gifts for Agu and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Wen richly rewarded Hong and sent his servant Gangge and others to Nanjing with letters and gifts for Agu and the others.

sentences.zh: 剛哥問合住何以知阿古等必從。

translations.literal: Gangge asked Hezhu how he knew Agu and the others would surely follow.
translations.idiomatic: Gangge asked Hezhu how he could be sure Agu and the others would follow.

sentences.zh: 合住曰：「阿古等與大王善，以此意其必從耳。」

translations.literal: Hezhu said: "Agu and the others are on good terms with His Highness; on that basis I suppose they will surely follow."
translations.idiomatic: Hezhu replied, "Agu and the others are on good terms with His Highness—that is why I assume they will follow."

sentences.zh: 剛哥到南京，見阿古等，不言其本來之事。

translations.literal: When Gangge reached Nanjing and met Agu and the others, he did not speak of the original matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Gangge reached Nanjing and met Agu and the others, he said nothing of the real purpose of his mission.

sentences.zh: 及還，紿文曰：「阿古從大王矣。」

translations.literal: On his return he deceived Wen, saying: "Agu has joined Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: On his return he lied to Wen, saying, "Agu has pledged himself to Your Highness."

sentences.zh: 文乃造兵仗，使家奴斡敵畫陣圖。

translations.literal: Wen then had weapons made and ordered his household slave Wudi to draw battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: Wen then had weapons manufactured and ordered his slave Wudi to draw battle formations.

sentences.zh: 家奴重喜詣河北東路上變，府遣總管判官孛特馳往德州捕文。

translations.literal: The household slave Zhongxi went to the Hebei East Route to report the plot; the prefecture sent chief administrator's aide Bete posthaste to De Prefecture to arrest Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The slave Zhongxi reported the plot to the Hebei East Route authorities, and the prefecture sent chief administrator's aide Bete posthaste to De Prefecture to arrest Wen.

sentences.zh: 孛特至德州，日已晚。

translations.literal: When Bete reached De Prefecture, the day was already late.
translations.idiomatic: Bete reached De Prefecture late in the day.

sentences.zh: 會文出獵，召防禦判官酬越謀就獵所執之。

translations.literal: It happened that Wen was out hunting; he summoned the defender's aide Chouyue to seize him at the hunting ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wen happened to be out hunting; Bete summoned the defender's aide Chouyue to seize him at the hunt.

sentences.zh: 酬越言：「文兵衛甚眾，且暮夜，明日文生日，可就會上執之。」

translations.literal: Chouyue said: "Wen's armed attendants are very numerous, and it is already evening; tomorrow is Wen's birthday—we can seize him at the gathering."
translations.idiomatic: Chouyue said, "Wen's armed attendants are numerous, and night is falling. Tomorrow is his birthday—we can seize him at the celebration."

sentences.zh: 孛特乃止。

translations.literal: Bete then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bete held off.

sentences.zh: 是夜，文知本府使至，意其事覺，乃與合住、忽裏者等俱亡去。

translations.literal: That night Wen learned that the prefectural envoy had arrived, guessed the affair was exposed, and fled together with Hezhu, Hulizhe, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: That night Wen learned the prefectural envoy had arrived, guessed the plot was exposed, and fled with Hezhu, Hulizhe, and the others.

sentences.zh: 河間府使奏文事，詔遣右司郎中紇石烈哲典、斡林修撰阿不罕訛裏也往德州鞫問。

translations.literal: The Hejian prefect reported Wen's case; an edict sent Right Department director Hesilie Zhe Dian and Hanlin compiler Abuhan Euliye to De Prefecture to interrogate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The Hejian prefect reported the case; an edict sent Right Department director Hesilie Zhe Dian and Hanlin compiler Abuhan Euliye to De Prefecture to conduct the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 上聞文亡命，謂宰臣曰：「海陵翦滅宗室殆盡，朕念太祖孫存者無幾人，曲為寬假，而文曾不知幸，尚懷異圖，何狂悖如此。」

translations.literal: When the sovereign heard that Wen had fled, he said to the chief ministers: "Hailing nearly exterminated the entire imperial clan. I thought of the Taizu's grandsons—few remain—and bent the rules to show leniency. Yet Wen did not know his good fortune and still harbored rebellious designs—how wildly perverse."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned Wen had fled, he told his chief ministers, "Hailing nearly wiped out the imperial clan. Of the Taizu's grandsons only a few remain, and I bent the rules to show them mercy. Yet Wen did not know his good fortune and still harbored treasonous designs—how wildly perverse."

sentences.zh: 上恐文久不獲，詿誤者多，督所在捕之。

translations.literal: The sovereign feared that if Wen were long uncaptured many would be misled, and urged every locality to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that if Wen remained at large many would be misled, he urged every locality to capture him.

sentences.zh: 詔募獲文者遷官五階，賜錢三千貫。

translations.literal: An edict offered promotion of five ranks and a grant of three thousand strings of cash to whoever captured Wen.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promised promotion of five ranks and three thousand strings of cash to whoever captured Wen.

sentences.zh: 文以大定十二年九月事覺，亡命凡四月，至十二月被獲，伏誅。

translations.literal: Wen's plot was exposed in the ninth month of the twelfth year of Dading; he was a fugitive for four months in all, and in the twelfth month was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot came to light in the ninth month of Dading 12; Wen was a fugitive for four months until captured in the twelfth month and executed.

sentences.zh: 康洪論死，餘皆坐如律。

translations.literal: Kang Hong was sentenced to death; the rest were punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Hong was sentenced to death; the rest were punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 詔釋其妻術實懶。

translations.literal: An edict released his wife Shushilan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict released his wife Shushilan.

sentences.zh: 孛特、酬越不即捕，致文亡去，孛特杖二百，除名，酬越杖一百，削兩階。

translations.literal: Because Bete and Chouyue did not arrest Wen at once and allowed him to escape, Bete received two hundred strokes of the staff and was struck from the rolls; Chouyue received one hundred strokes and was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Because Bete and Chouyue had not arrested Wen immediately and let him escape, Bete received two hundred strokes of the staff and was struck from the rolls; Chouyue received one hundred strokes and was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「德州防禦使文、北京曹貴、鄜州李方皆因術士妄談祿命，陷於大戮。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The defender of De Prefecture Wen, Cao Gui of the Northern Capital, and Li Fang of Fu Prefecture all fell into capital punishment because diviners recklessly spoke of fortune and fate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Defender Wen of De Prefecture, Cao Gui of the Northern Capital, and Li Fang of Fu Prefecture all went to their deaths because diviners recklessly spoke of fortune and fate.

sentences.zh: 凡術士多務苟得，肆為異說。

translations.literal: Diviners for the most part pursue quick gain and freely spread strange doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners for the most part chase quick profit and spread reckless doctrines.

sentences.zh: 自今宗室、宗女有屬籍者及官職三品者，除占問嫁娶、修造、葬事，不得推算相命，違者徒二年，重者從重。」

translations.literal: From now on, for imperial clansmen and clan women on the registers and for officials of the third rank and above, except for divination on marriage, construction, and burial, fortune-telling and fate-reading are forbidden; violators are sentenced to two years' penal servitude, and in serious cases punished more heavily."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth members of the imperial clan on the registers and officials of the third rank and above may consult diviners only for marriage, construction, and burial; fortune-telling and fate-reading are otherwise forbidden. Violators are sentenced to two years' penal servitude, with heavier penalties for graver cases."

sentences.zh: 上以文家財產賜其故兄特進齊之子咬住，並以西京留守京沒入家產賜之。

translations.literal: The sovereign granted Wen's family property to Yaozhu, son of his late elder brother the Tejin Qi, and also gave him the confiscated estates of Jing, the Western Capital garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted Wen's family property to Yaozhu, son of his late elder brother the Tejin Qi, and also gave him the confiscated estates of Jing, the Western Capital garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宗望啟行平州，戰勝白河，席捲而南，風行電舉，兵無留難，再閱月而汴京圍矣。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Zong Wang set out from Ping Prefecture, won at the White River, swept south like a wind or lightning bolt—the army met no delay; within two months Bianjing was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Zong Wang marched from Ping Prefecture, won at the White River, and swept south like wind and lightning—the army met no check; within two months Bianjing was under siege.

sentences.zh: 所謂敵不能與校者耶。

translations.literal: Was this not what is called an enemy who could not stand comparison?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not a foe who could not stand against him?

sentences.zh: 既取信德，留兵守之，以為後距，此豈輕者耶。

translations.literal: Having taken Xinde, he left troops to guard it as a rear base—was this a light matter?
translations.idiomatic: Having taken Xinde, he left troops to hold it as a rear base—was that a small thing?

sentences.zh: 《管子》曰：「徑于絕地，攻於恃固，獨出獨入，而莫之能止。」

translations.literal: The Guanzi says: "He marches through desperate ground, attacks where the enemy relies on strength, goes out and comes in alone, and none can stop him."
translations.idiomatic: The Guanzi says: "He marches through desperate ground, strikes where the enemy trusts in strength, goes out and comes in alone, and none can stop him."

sentences.zh: 其宗望之謂乎。

translations.literal: Is this not what is meant by Zong Wang?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not Zong Wang?
